summary: Katie Price's estranged husband, Lee Andrews, sent a bizarre WhatsApp voice note to Good Morning Britain hosts from a Dubai prison, offering them £10,000 in cryptocurrency. Andrews canceled a joint studio appearance regarding claims that he lied about being a crypto-multimillionaire after Price discovered only £2.22 in his wallet. During her appearance on the show, Price confirmed their split and stated that she felt scammed by him.
key_points: Lee Andrews offered Ed Balls and Susanna Reid up to £10,000 in cryptocurrency via a WhatsApp voice note.
Andrews claimed he could not appear on Good Morning Britain because he is being held in a Dubai prison over unpaid debts.
Price revealed she discovered Andrews's crypto wallet contained only £2.22, leading to accusations that he lied about his wealth.
Andrews denied the scamming allegations, claiming he has 50 million USDT in legitimate funds.
Katie Price confirmed her separation from Andrews during her interview on the ITV show.

title: 70 Up review – a deeply moving conclusion for the 63-year-long TV experiment
author: Lucy Mangan
content:
And so the great experiment begun by Granada Television in 1964 is over. That year, Seven Up! introduced the viewing public to 14 primary school children – 10 boys and four girls from a range of backgrounds – who would become part of an ongoing documentary project that returned to film them at regular intervals and interrogate the truth of the Jesuitical motto “Give me the child for the first seven years and I will give you the man”.
Seven Up!, part of ITV’s flagship World in Action series, was directed by Paul Almond but thereafter the enterprise became synonymous with Michael Apted, who originally helped find the children and took over the making of the programmes. He died in 2021, two years after completing 63 Up. It had been thought the series would end there but when one of the participants, Nick Hitchon – a Yorkshire farmer’s son who grew up to be a nuclear scientist – called one of the team to say that he had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and wanted to give one last interview, a final episode was commissioned.
Directed by Asif Kapadia, it has a more reflective and elegiac tone than in previous years. Lynn, who spent most of her life as a devoted children’s librarian – council funds and cuts permitting – died in 2013. Almost everyone else is retired. Everyone is looking back. Jackie speaks with great relief of the calm and relative solitude in which she now lives, having moved away from the family that – reading between the lines – she clearly loves but required much from her. The three prep school boys, John, Charles and Andrew, first seen perched on the sofa in their headteacher’s study and talking with disarming sweetness about futures at Charterhouse, the Dragon and Oxbridge, have had the lives of privilege and ease that they expected and that we expected for them. Andrew wishes he had spent more time with his family. “School plays,” he says. “Sports days.” There are shades of similar regret from some of the other men, too. But the Up series has always had to sacrifice the interrogation of such detail for breadth of coverage, and this is one of the many potentially fruitful paths you wish had been travelled further down.
Tony, the self-described “Little Artful Dodger” and would-be jockey turned cab driver remains as irrepressible as ever, though he notes his biggest mistake was deciding not to commit to the former career after his mentor warned him that he would struggle to meet the necessary weight all his life. Bruce has retired from teaching and now sings in the local choir, walks his dog on the beach and volunteers with the local branch of the RNLI. The thoughtful, gentle, Christian boy has become a thoughtful, gentle, Christian man.
Symon, the terribly sad-eyed boy brought up in a children’s home (“What you don’t have, you don’t miss,” he said at 14, and it was so nakedly untrue that you still have to look away when they show this moving scene again here) has fostered more than 100 children with his second wife over the last 20 years. He looks happier now. The children are welcomed back for visits all the time. Paul, Symon’s companion in the children’s home, has built himself a good life in Australia. He is a grandfather now. “Family is 100% the main thing.”
![‘I’m probably as happy as I can be’ … Neil.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/ee4036bcc9f8e5fd7c867d632011635fef730d79/164_0_2815_2252/master/2815.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Neil – the perky, bright Liverpudlian schoolboy who dreamed of Oxford but has struggled with depression all his life, and experienced periods of homelessness in between being a local councillor and lay minister and, briefly, a husband – now lives alone in France. The perkiness left long ago but he is as thoughtful, articulate and unassuming as ever. He is clearly still vulnerable in many ways and his existence precarious, but he has found a way of being that brings him contentment enough. Yes, he says, he is sometimes lonely. “But that is a characteristic of the age … I’m probably as happy as I can be, given my life.”
There is, especially in the second instalment of this final film, something of a meta-narrative too, as the participants give their thoughts about the series and about Apted. We also hear archive footage of Apted reflecting on what he learned over the years. Jackie was perhaps his earliest and most vocal combatant, challenging him over various questions – largely about marriage and sex – that she said he only dared ask the women, and she pulls him up on his class bias too. John describes him as having “a sneering and somewhat supercilious manner” and, in essence, painting the privileged as bogeymen. Apted himself said he was judgmental at the beginning, and gradually taught himself to stay out of things as much as possible. But it remains clear, 60-odd years on, that this was not a rigorous or objective journalistic venture but a series profoundly shaped by one man’s vision, background and baked-in assumptions. Acknowledging this, as Kapadia does, is the best thing to do with it now. The achievement has become an artefact to be admired, still, but questioned too.
summary: The landmark documentary series that followed 14 British children from 1964 reaches its conclusion with a final episode directed by Asif Kapadia. Commissioned after participant Nick Hitchon was diagnosed with terminal cancer, the episode offers a reflective look at the participants in their retirement years. The final installment features updates on the surviving subjects, including Neil, Tony, Bruce, and Symon, while also examining the complicated legacy of longtime director Michael Apted.
key_points: The 63-year documentary experiment concludes with a final episode directed by Asif Kapadia, originally prompted by participant Nick Hitchon's terminal cancer diagnosis.
The final instalment provides reflective updates on the surviving participants, most of whom are now retired and looking back on their lives.
Participants such as Jackie and John offer critiques of longtime director Michael Apted, highlighting his class bias and personal assumptions.
The series is recognized not as a purely objective journalistic venture, but as an influential television artefact shaped by Apted's vision.

title: 'The Celebrity Traitors' Trailer: First Glimpse Of Bella Ramsey & More
author: Jake Kanter
content:
Let the backstabbing begin! The Celebrity Traitors is confirmed to return to the BBC next month.
The eagerly anticipated series will premiere on October 1 (not September 23 as originally speculated) on BBC One and iPlayer, with a stacked cast including Bella Ramsey, Maya Jama, and Richard E. Grant.
To mark the premiere date, the BBC has released a new trailer, with the celebrities getting their game face on in the Scottish Highlands.
“The game is on,” intones host Claudia Winkleman. “There are now killers among you.”
Watch on Deadline
The full cast includes Amol Rajan, Bella Ramsey, James Acaster, James Blunt, Jerry Hall, Joanne McNally, Joe Lycett, Julie Hesmondhalgh, King Kenny, Leigh-Anne Pinnock, Maya Jama, Michael Sheen, Miranda Hart, Myha’la, Professor Hannah Fry, Richard E. Grant, Rob Beckett, Romesh Ranganathan, Ross Kemp, Sebastian Croft and Sharon Rooney.
Speaking at the Edinburgh TV Festival last month, BBC content chief Kate Phillips revealed that there will be tears and surprises in the new season.
Season 1 of The Celebrity Traitors was the most-watched show on British TV last year. It debuted on BBC iPlayer and BBC One in October 2025 and was seen by an average audience of 14.9M, with a peak of 15.4M for the finale. Comedian Alan Carr emerged victorious in a game that featured Stephen Fry and Celia Imrie.
The Celebrity Traitors is produced by Studio Lambert Scotland for BBC One and iPlayer and has been commissioned by Kalpna Patel-Knight, Head of Entertainment Commissioning for the BBC.
The executive producers for All3Media-backed Studio Lambert are Mike Cotton, Sarah Fay, Lewis Thurlow and Katy Fox, with production executives, Lynette Woods-Reynolds, Gemma Scholes and Faye Donaldson. The commissioning editors for the BBC are Neil McCallum and Michael Jochnowitz.
The Traitors (Dutch title: De Verraders) was created and developed by IDTV in cooperation with RTL Creative Unit. All3Media International is global partner for The Traitors and handles format and tape sales worldwide.
summary: The BBC has released a new trailer for The Celebrity Traitors, confirming that the series will premiere on October 1 on BBC One and iPlayer. Hosted by Claudia Winkleman, the upcoming season features a stacked celebrity cast filmed in the Scottish Highlands. Season 1 was the most-watched show on British TV last year, drawing an average audience of 14.9 million viewers.
key_points: The Celebrity Traitors premieres on October 1 on BBC One and iPlayer.
The new season is hosted by Claudia Winkleman and filmed in the Scottish Highlands.
The cast features numerous celebrities including Bella Ramsey, Maya Jama, and Richard E. Grant.
Season 1 was the most-watched show on British TV last year with an average audience of 14.9 million.

title: All supporting acts withdraw from Ed Sheeran’s tour in solidarity with Macklemore
author: Adrian Horton
content:
All four supporting acts for upcoming dates of Ed Sheeran’s Loop tour have withdrawn in solidarity with fellow opening act Macklemore, as backlash grows to his removal from the tour over onstage comments in support of Palestine.
Finneas, the singer who was scheduled to open for Sheeran on six South American dates in November, withdrew from the tour on Tuesday afternoon, hours after Sheeran posted his own lengthy statement to Instagram explaining pressure from venue owners to remove Macklemore for pro-Palestine comments made during two shows at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium.
In a two-minute speech on 4 September, the Grammy-winning artist told the audience he wanted the people of Gaza and “the occupied West Bank” to know “we have not forgotten about them”, along with the words “free Palestine”. The remark prompted a petition calling for Macklemore’s removal from the tour from the Israeli American Council and the opposition of some venue owners – including Robert Kraft, the billionaire owner of the New England Patriots and a prominent donor to Israel.
“Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed,” Finneas wrote on social media. “I have decided to withdraw from my upcoming tour dates with Ed Sheeran. I stand with Palestine and its people.”
The decision came shortly after Aaron Rowe, an Irish singer who opened for Sheeran in Australia earlier this year and was scheduled for the 10 remaining dates in North America, announced his own withdrawal from the tour. “I don’t take the decision lightly,” he wrote on Instagram. “Ed has been a friends to me and has changed my life, I could never thank him enough for this.
“But as Irish people we know all too well about genocide, forced famine and violent occupation. I cannot stand by and allow billionaires to use their position of power to silence the rightful voices of those who speak up against Israeli genocide and who highlight the savage murder of children. I would lose all respect for myself to carry on as normal.”
The Irish band Beoga shortly after joined Rowe in departing the US tour to protest the “silencing of Macklemore by zionist lobbies”.
“We are a traditional Irish band who never saw ourselves playing in stadiums of that size and that opportunity is not lost on us,” they wrote on social media. “We have been friends with Ed for over 10 years now and will continue to be. We believe in dialogue as a means of progressing the plight of the Palestinian people.”
The Danish pop band Lukas Graham also dropped out of the tour on Tuesday afternoon. “We should be able to speak about war, about civilians being killed, about children who deserve to grow up. Wherever they live. Whatever flag flies over them,” wrote lead singer Lukas Forchhammer on the band’s social media. “Money doesn’t give you the right to own the conversation. Nobody’s bank balance should decide who gets to speak or which suffering we’re allowed to acknowledge.”
The abrupt withdrawals of the Sheeran’s opening acts came hours after the English singer confirmed that Kraft, along with several other stadium owners, refused to allow the tour to play at their venues if Macklemore continued to open for him. Though Sheeran wrote that the was “appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine” and “the suffering and pain caused on both sides,” he said that attempts to broker conversations between parties was unsuccessful, and the “venue’s and the promoter’s decision was final”.
“Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision, it was not mine,” he wrote in a multi-page post on Instagram. “I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living.”
“I have spent this week trying to build bridges, to find a solution and unfortunately, was unable to do so,” he concluded. “I know who I am, both as a person and as an artist, and those who know my heart know my values too.”
The tour withdrawals join a growing chorus of backlash to Macklemore’s removal, including numerous politicians and Ms Rachel, the children’s educator and Youtube star, who wrote on Instagram: “Ed Sheeran had an opportunity [to] show that we won’t be bullied into punishing people for supporting Palestine. Instead he caved to people who refuse to accept what the world knows. A genocide is happening in Gaza. We all need to speak on it.”
Kehlani, the singer whose pro-Palestine activism led to the cancellation of a concert at Cornell University last year, commented on social media in support of Macklemore: “A LOT of the venues / owners are rallied together this way. honored to know you brother.”
In his own statement on Monday, Kraft did not deny refusing to allow Macklemore on stage at his Gillette Stadium outside Boston, and said the decision was based on both Macklemore’s “recent actions” and “a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community”.
“I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same – peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate,” he said.
summary: All four supporting acts for Ed Sheeran's upcoming tour dates have withdrawn in solidarity after Macklemore was removed from the lineup due to his pro-Palestine stage remarks. Sheeran stated that venue owners and promoters, including Robert Kraft, forced the decision, refusing to let the tour play if Macklemore remained. Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Beoga, and Lukas Graham all pulled out of their scheduled appearances, criticizing the silencing of artists speaking out against the conflict in Gaza.
key_points: Macklemore was removed from Ed Sheeran's tour following a petition and pressure from venue owners over his pro-Palestine remarks at MetLife Stadium.
Supporting acts Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Beoga, and Lukas Graham all withdrew from their scheduled tour dates in solidarity with Macklemore.
Ed Sheeran stated that removing Macklemore was the final decision of promoters and venue owners, and that his own attempts to broker a compromise were unsuccessful.
Robert Kraft defended the venue's stance, citing Macklemore's recent actions and a broader history of allegedly offensive rhetoric.
The withdrawals drew widespread attention and criticism from other public figures regarding the suppression of artists speaking about the conflict.

title: Ed Sheeran responds to backlash over removing Macklemore from tour after ‘Free Palestine’ comments
author: Adrian Horton
content:
Singer Ed Sheeran has responded to the backlash over the removal of Macklemore from his North American Loop tour, following the rapper’s “Free Palestine” speech on stage at MetLife stadium in New Jersey.
In a two-minute speech on 4 September, the Grammy-winning artist told the audience he wanted the people of Gaza and “the occupied West Bank” to know “we have not forgotten about them”, prompting owners of subsequent stadium tour venues – including Robert Kraft, the billionaire owner of the New England Patriots and a prominent supporter of and donor to Israel – to object to Macklemore’s appearance on the tour.
Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the US leg of Sheeran’s tour, confirmed Macklemore’s removal from the eight planned subsequent dates on Monday; hours later, Macklemore posted a lengthy statement reiterating his support of Palestine and the people of Gaza and outlining conversations about political activism with Sheeran, prompting criticism of the English singer’s apolitical stance and, on Tuesday afternoon, the withdrawal of another opening act.
On Tuesday, Sheeran responded with a lengthy Instagram post captioned: “It’s important that I set out some facts.”
“I am appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine,” he wrote in the first of several bullet-point statements. “The suffering and pain caused on both sides is a human tragedy. There are too many wars across the world causing immeasurable pain, none of which should be tolerated.”
According to Sheeran, Macklemore “asked to join my tour last year and I agreed, because I respect him as an artist”. He went on to say that he allowed the Thrift Shop singer to perform a set list of his choosing, “as with all my support acts”.
The Seattle-bred rapper, long an outspoken supporter of the rights of Palestinians and people in Gaza, delivered the brief remarks between songs during his first appearance on tour.
“A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: free Palestine,” he said. “I said: free Palestine! I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them.”
He also played his protest anthem Hind’s Hall, which celebrated protesters’ occupation of a building they named in honor of Hind Rajab, a six-year-old killed by the Israeli military in 2024, accompanied by images of the Israeli military’s destruction of Gaza, which has killed more than 75,000 people in 16 months, according to some estimates.
At the second of his appearances at MetLife on 5 September, Macklemore reiterated his support for Palestine and addressed Jewish members of the audience: “Criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide in no way is a criticism of you. My message is for peace, love; for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect and equality.”
Following those comments, which prompted the Israeli American Council to launch a petition calling for Macklemore’s removal from the tour, US venues communicated to Sheeran that they would refuse to host the show if the rapper was still a supporting act.
“I was informed this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said,” he wrote. Though Sheeran said that he attempted to broker conversations among the promoters, venue owners such as Kraft and activists “on both sides”, the “venue’s and the promoter’s decision was final”.
“Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision, it was not mine,” he said. “I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living.”
Sheeran went on to outline his larger view on the use of his platform, which Macklemore had described the day prior as “his typical apolitical stance” that “was being challenged in a way it had never been before”.
after newsletter promotion
“I have always used my platform and music to bring people from all backgrounds and cultures together and this won’t ever change,” he wrote, later adding: “I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep the conversations open, not closed.”
“I am not complicit,” he added. “I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean that I don’t care. Nor does it mean that I don’t support causes in my own, personal way.”
“I have spent this week trying to build bridges, to find a solution and unfortunately, was unable to do so,” Sheeran concluded his post. “I know who I am, both as a person and as an artist, and those who know my heart know my values too.”
Hours after Sheeran issued his statement, Aaron Rowe, the Irish musician scheduled to open for Sheeran for his 10 remaining US shows, announced that he would be withdrawing from the tour. “I don’t take the decision lightly,” he wrote on Instagram. “Ed has been a friend to me and has changed my life, I could never thank him enough for this.
“But as Irish people we know all too well about genocide, forced famine and violent occupation. I cannot stand by and allow billionaires to use their position of power to silence the rightful voices of those who speak up against Israeli genocide and who highlight the savage murder of children. I would lose all respect for myself to carry on as normal.”
He concluded: “I need to be true to myself and my ancestors who resisted colonisation, and fought for a freedom that I enjoy today in Ireland. Free Palestine.”
As of now, the North American leg of Sheeran’s tour will conclude without Rowe in November at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida, which earlier this year hosted two shows by Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, who has a history of antisemitic statements.
summary: Ed Sheeran responded to backlash regarding the removal of Macklemore from his North American tour following the rapper's "Free Palestine" stage remarks. Sheeran stated that the decision to drop Macklemore was made by the tour promoters and venue owners, such as billionaire Robert Kraft, after objections to how the message was conveyed. In his response, Sheeran defended his apolitical public stance and emphasized his personal view of the conflict as a human tragedy. Following the controversy, another opening act, Aaron Rowe, also withdrew from the tour.
key_points: Macklemore was removed from eight upcoming dates on Ed Sheeran's North American tour after voicing support for Palestine at MetLife Stadium.
US venue owners and the Messina Touring Group made the final decision to remove Macklemore after objections were raised.
Ed Sheeran stated on Instagram that the removal was not his decision and defended his choice to maintain a personal approach to activism.
Irish musician Aaron Rowe subsequently withdrew from his role as an opening act for the remainder of the tour.
The tour is set to conclude in November in Tampa, Florida.

title: Zendaya leads star-studded Emmys
author: Kelly-Anne Taylor
content:
![Zendaya wore a semi-sheer crystal-embellished gown for the award ceremony in LA](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503083818_17894524541290_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqVfKYF8F8biotmZZgOU3KX34ihL9D5G77hk2Gx25ScXg.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Zendaya wore a semi-sheer crystal-embellished gown for the award ceremony in LA](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503083818_17894524541290_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqVfKYF8F8biotmZZgOU3KX34ihL9D5G77hk2Gx25ScXg.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Unsurprisingly, the biggest night in television pulled in a star-studded crowd. The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards, hosted in Los Angeles, saw Hollywood celebrities get their glad rags on for the chance to win a gong for their work on the small screen.
Zendaya, nominated for outstanding lead actress in a drama series for her role in Euphoria, arrived in a semi-sheer crystal gown. Florence Pugh, who will star in a forthcoming Netflix series based on John Steinbeck’s East of Eden, made her Emmys debut in an off-the-shoulder lilac dress.
![Florence Pugh wore a lilac Vivienne Westwood dress](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503086368_17894509634652_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqcTSUi9vmp6xDmpMhvK6AOTIg_UJUfaXZgg_L3G-w1c.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
![Nicole Kidman, Dakota Fanning, Michelle Pfeiffer and Elle Fanning (left to right) at the award show](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503092358_17894509632034_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqU7XSZWUScsha0PBU9PW8gwOqsesN1C8MjbMuR6Sr2OY.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Taylor Swift also made a surprise appearance in a pre-recorded Law & Order skit, starring as a detective alongside Mariska Hargitay, the Emmy’s host who is best known for her small-screen role as Captain Olivia Benson. She was the first woman to host the award ceremony in 15 years.
![Taylor Swift made a surprise virtual cameo alongside Mariska Hargitay](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503097883_17894518506030_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Matthew Rhys, the Welsh actor, became the first person to win two lead acting awards in one night. He took home the gong for best lead actor in a limited series for Netflix’s psychological thriller The Beast in Me, as well as best lead actor in a comedy for Apple TV’s Widow’s Bay.
Rhys dedicated his second award to the “great and good people of Wales”. Backstage, he added: “I’m from a small country, and I’m glad we get moments to put our flag on the map and say ‘we punch higher than our weight sometimes’.”
![Matthew Rhys won two lead actor awards on Monday night](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503117300_17894525845930_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq5E09dxZpf6m97andAsHWytbAInUh0uzNuArb_jHy9S4.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Kate O’Flynn, Rhys’ Widow’s Bay co-star and a self-professed “Lancashire Lass”, also scooped up the award for best supporting comedy actress.
![Kate O'Flynn accepting her award for outstanding supporting actress in a comedy series](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503114574_17894528227650_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Alan Cumming, the Scottish TV presenter, accepted the best reality show award for the US version of The Traitors. It was an evening light on political messages, but Cumming used his acceptance speech to call for US citizens to register to vote before the midterm elections in November.
![Alan Cumming accepted the award for best reality show for the US version of The Traitors](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503098229_17894509635325_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf_4Xpit_DMGvdp2n7FDd82k.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Saul Metzstein picked up the award for outstanding director for Apple TV’s Slow Horses. Gary Oldman, who stars as spymaster Jackson Lamb, and Jack Lowden, who plays agent River Cartwright in the adaptation of Mick Heron’s espionage novels, were also both nominated for awards.
Other big winners of the evening included HBO’s medical drama The Pitt, which won best drama series. The series’ lead actor Noah Wyle also took home an award.
Jean Smart made history with a fifth consecutive win for her role as Deborah Vance in HBO’s Hacks.
![Selena Gomez wore a gold Louis Vuitton dress to the ceremony on Monday night](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/en-us/news/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503081134_17894509631316_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq2aizoQ_BaLt4dX785YMTtZgojZYlP8f0i9h2tPqCNsM.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Michael J Fox, the Canadian actor, was the recipient of the Bob Hope Humanitarian award. The actor spoke about being “handed a role I wasn’t looking for” – a reference to his Parkinson’s diagnosis at 29 – and his fear of the public’s reaction.
In his acceptance speech, he said he was moved by the support he had received and proud of the progress he had made to “eradicate this disease forever” through his organisation The Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research.
Sally Field, who starred in Steel Magnolias alongside Dolly Parton, led a touching tribute to the country music legend, who died last month.
Field described Parton as “genuine, humble, supportive and blisteringly funny” adding: “She was a humanitarian whose contribution has made a profound difference across our country.”
summary: The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards in Los Angeles brought together television stars for a night of historic wins and notable appearances. Matthew Rhys made history by winning two lead acting awards in a single night, while Jean Smart secured her fifth consecutive win for Hacks. The ceremony also featured emotional tributes, including Michael J. Fox receiving the Bob Hope Humanitarian award and Sally Field honoring the late Dolly Parton.
key_points: Matthew Rhys became the first person to win two lead acting awards in one night for his roles in The Beast in Me and Widow’s Bay.
Jean Smart made history with a fifth consecutive win for her role in HBO’s Hacks.
Michael J. Fox received the Bob Hope Humanitarian award and spoke about his Parkinson's diagnosis and foundation.
Taylor Swift made a surprise pre-recorded appearance in a Law & Order skit alongside host Mariska Hargitay.
Sally Field led a tribute to country music legend Dolly Parton, who passed away the previous month.

title: Emmys 2026: Widow’s Bay dominates as Matthew Rhys and Jean Smart land historic wins
author: Sian Cain
content:
Matthew Rhys has become the first actor in 78 years of Emmys history to win multiple lead actor awards for performances in different shows in the same year, for Widow’s Bay and The Beast in Me.
The 51-year-old Welsh actor won outstanding lead actor in a comedy for Apple TV’s Widow’s Bay and outstanding lead actor in a limited series for his role in Netflix’s The Beast in Me at the ceremony on Monday night. With his 2018 win of outstanding lead actor in a drama for The Americans, he is the first male performer to win all three lead acting categories.
During his speech for his Widow’s Bay win, Rhys thanked “the great and good people of Wales, who were as much a nurturer as anyone else. We are a small but mighty nation. This is incredible.”
“I am slightly giddy and a little bit dizzy,” he told media after his historic win. “I genuinely can’t believe it. I hope to reflect on it tomorrow. At the moment, I genuinely can’t quite believe what has happened.”
He said he had not expected he would win for The Beast in Me: “That was such a shock, as I am sure you could tell from the rambling speech I gave … a vomit of a speech.”
Widow’s Bay dominated the ceremony in Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater, winning 14 of 19 nominations, including best comedy series, supporting actress in a comedy for Kate O’Flynn, supporting actor for Stephen Root, as well as best writing for its creator, Katie Dippold, and best director for Hiro Murai.
![Noah Wyle](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/88da6b0941d0f24a04ccae2c7f71430621111ecc/391_0_4009_3208/master/4009.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
In other categories, The Pitt won outstanding drama series and outstanding lead actor in a drama for Noah Wyle. The medical drama lead this year’s nominee tally with 25, winning six.
Wyle, the first drama actor to win consecutive Emmys since Bryan Cranston on Breaking Bad, spoke about his roots. “I grew up in LA,” he said. “I’m a Hollywood kid. I was raised on a television, and movie theaters were my place of worship. This is all I’ve ever wanted to do, and this is the only club I’ve ever wanted to join. Thank you for accepting me.”
Jean Smart and Alison Janney both won their eighth acting Emmys, tying for the most acting Emmy wins with Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Cloris Leachman. Janney won best supporting actress for The Diplomat, while Smart won her fifth outstanding lead actress in a comedy Emmy for her performance as Deborah Vance in the fifth and final season of Hacks, becoming the first woman to win an Emmy for every season of a show.
![Jean Smart with her fifth Emmy for Hacks](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/4292806693ef3914d6627a0864a8bb11c910304d/248_0_2505_2004/master/2505.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
In the drama categories, Rhea Seehorn won best lead actress for Pluribus, her first Emmy win, while Tom Pelphrey won best supporting actor for Task, in a category stacked with actors from The Pitt.
DTF St Louis dominated the limited or anthology series categories with seven wins, including best series, supporting actor for David Harbour and supporting actress for Linda Cardellini.
After the controversial cancellation of The Late Show, Stephen Colbert won the Emmy for a variety show for the show’s final season. Colbert thanked “the over 200 people” who worked on the show over a decade – and used his speech to spruik their talents. “Hire them,” he told the room. “They will make your day better and your lives easier.”
The ceremony was relatively light on politics compared with previous years. Accepting best writing in a drama for Pluribus, the show’s creator, Vince Gilligan, described the show as set in a world “in which everybody gets along – that’s so sci-fi. But think about it: there’s nothing weirder than our current reality.”
“We will never agree on everything, but we can treat each other with respect,” he said, “and we can stop listening to a relative few who think that is for suckers.”
The Pitt’s creator, R Scott Gemmill, while accepting the best drama award, told the room: “It is so hard to tell what is real and what we can believe any more, which makes telling honest stories about real human struggles so much more important than ever. What you do, it changes people’s lives.”
Nominated shows that came away empty-handed during the ceremony included Shrinking, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, Beef, Margo’s Got Money Troubles, Abbott Elementary and Paradise.
summary: At the 2026 Emmys, Matthew Rhys made history by winning two lead actor awards in the same year for different shows, while Widow's Bay dominated the ceremony with 14 wins. Other notable winners included Noah Wyle for The Pitt and Jean Smart, who won her fifth Emmy for Hacks. Shows like The Pitt and DTF St Louis also secured major category wins.
key_points: Matthew Rhys won outstanding lead actor in a comedy for Widow's Bay and in a limited series for The Beast in Me, becoming the first actor to win multiple lead acting awards in different shows in the same year.
Widow's Bay dominated the ceremony at the Peacock Theater, winning 14 of its 19 nominations, including best comedy series.
Noah Wyle won outstanding lead actor in a drama for The Pitt, making him the first drama actor to win consecutive Emmys since Bryan Cranston.
Jean Smart won her fifth Emmy for Hacks, becoming the first woman to win an award for every season of a show, and tied with Alison Janney for eight total career acting Emmys.
DTF St Louis won seven awards in the limited or anthology categories, including best series.

title: Emmy Awards: Welsh actor Matthew Rhys makes history with double win
author: Ian Youngs; Steven McIntosh
content:
Watch: Highlights from the 2026 Emmy Awards, a star-studded and record-breaking night
- Published
Welsh actor Matthew Rhys has made history at the Emmy Awards, becoming the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night.
Rhys was recognised at the prestigious US ceremony for his roles in supernatural TV comedy Widow's Bay and psychological thriller The Beast In Me.
On stage, Rhys dedicated his second award "to the great and good people of Wales, who were as much a nurture as anyone else".
"We are a small but mighty nation. This is incredible," he said, adding "Diolch yn fawr iawn" - which means "thank you very much" in Welsh.
Other winners of the coveted US TV awards included Jean Smart, Allison Janney and Stephen Colbert, while there was an emotional tribute to Dolly Parton and a special humanitarian award for Michael J Fox.
Watch: Selena Gomez, Zendaya and other stars light up Emmys red carpet
Proud Rhys flies the flag
Rhys was named best lead actor in a limited series for The Beast In Me, then won best lead actor in a comedy for Widow's Bay.
A small number of actors, including Alan Alda, Sally Field, John Goodman, Elisabeth Moss and Ted Danson, have previously been nominated for two lead acting prizes in the same year, but Rhys is the first to score a double win.
Backstage, he said: "I'm from a small country, and I'm glad we get moments to kind of put our flag on the map and say, 'we punch higher than our weight sometimes'."
![Matthew Rhys and Keri Russell](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/c1f8/live/817a3690-b0b7-11f1-b8f0-8f0427d95d2f.jpg)
Rhys attended the ceremony with his partner, US actress Keri Russell, who was also nominated for an Emmy
The Beast In Me follows a grieving author, played by Claire Danes, who becomes obsessed with a mysterious new neighbour suspected of murder.
Rhys said it was a "real shock" to win the award, and told Danes: "Thank you for letting me join the mystery machine and bringing out the beast, you are an intimidating scene partner, but I'm grateful for all this."
Later in the night, accepting the comedy actor prize for playing the mayor in Widow's Bay, he thanked the family, friends and colleagues who supported his career, including his parents who "kicked me on to the stage at a very early age".
A win for 'Lancashire lass'
![Kate O'Flynn wins the Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series Award for "Widow's Bay" at the 78th Emmy Awards held at Peacock Theater on September 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/563d/live/15d89e10-b0ab-11f1-a540-61c3f7fc4e6c.jpg)
Kate O'Flynn thanked Widow's Bay producers for "trusting this Lancashire lass"
His Widow's Bay co-star Kate O'Flynn was among the other British winners, being named best supporting comedy actress for playing Patricia in the show about a fictional island beset by a centuries-old curse.
"I want to thank our mayor and all the residents of Widow's Bay, in front and behind the camera," said O'Flynn, from Bury in Greater Manchester.
She added: "This is the role of a lifetime... Thank you for trusting this Lancashire lass to play a sassy broad like Patricia."
Smart and Janney equal Emmys record
![Jean Smart and Allison Janney pose backstage at the Emmy Awards, against a purple background](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/cdf0/live/76cbe120-b0b8-11f1-b1d1-571ed4d7ff2c.jpg)
Jean Smart and Allison Janney equalled the same Emmys record, minutes apart
Elsewhere, Jean Smart won best comedy actress for her role in the fifth and final series of Hacks.
It is the fifth Emmy she has won for the Hollywood satire. "What a ride this has been," Smart reflected, and joked that the audience only gave her a standing ovation "because I'm old".
It was Smart's eighth Emmy win in total, and The Diplomat's Allison Janney also picked up the eighth Emmy of her career, scoring best supporting actress in a drama series.
Smart and Janney have both now equalled the record for the most acting wins ever, shared with Cloris Leachman and Julia Louis-Dreyfus.
Despite her past success, Janney was a surprise winner on Monday and said she was "genuinely shocked" to see off competition from four stars of hospital drama The Pitt, among others.
Meanwhile, Rhea Seehorn won the first Emmy of her career for best lead actress in a drama series for Pluribus, the Apple TV show about a woman who discovers almost everyone else in the world has been taken over by a mysterious mind virus.
The Pitt scores top prize
![Noah Wyle accepts the Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series Award for "The Pitt" onstage during the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards at Peacock Theater on September 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/b60d/live/952e2cc0-b0b0-11f1-b1d1-571ed4d7ff2c.jpg)
Noah Wyle has won best lead actor in a drama series for two consecutive years
The Pitt won best drama, traditionally seen as the most prestigious award of the night.
And the show's leading star Noah Wyle also picked up the trophy for best lead actor in a drama series for the second year in a row.
"I'm a Hollywood kid. I was raised on a television, and movie theaters were my place of worship," Wyle told the audience. "This is all I've ever wanted to do and this is the only club I've ever wanted to join. Thank you for accepting me."
The former ER star praised all of his fellow nominees, but singled out veteran British star Sir Gary Oldman, who was nominated for Slow Horses.
Wyle said he was inspired by Sir Gary's performance as Sex Pistols bassist Sid Vicious in 1986 film Sid and Nancy, recalling how at the time he thought it was "the benchmark that I want to hit one day in my career".
Hero's welcome for Michael J Fox
![Michael J Fox at the 78th Emmy Awards held at Peacock Theater on September 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/99ff/live/03f836c0-b0af-11f1-b1d1-571ed4d7ff2c.jpg)
Michael J Fox was nominated for his guest role in Shrinking as well as receiving the honorary humanitarian accolade
Michael J Fox was given a standing ovation as he received the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award for his campaigning for support for Parkinson's disease.
The Back to the Future star, 65, who founded the Michael J Fox Foundation in 2000, said: "When it starts getting tough, you show up, you help, and if you get a little joy while you're doing it, that's even better."
Appearing in a wheelchair, he told the audience he initially kept his condition secret after being diagnosed at the age of 29.
"I worried that it would affect my work and my relationships with audiences when they laughed if they knew I was sick," he said.
But he added: "Eventually, I understood that accepting Parkinson's didn't mean I had to surrender to it. It just meant doing what I could for everyone living with this disease. So I set out to advocate for patients' needs and raise money, and to propel us towards a cure."
Dolly Parton tribute
![US singer Reba McEntire sings a tribute to Dolly Parton during the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards at the Peacock Theatre at LA Live in Los Angeles on September 14, 2026](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/aac2/live/bd3194d0-b0ad-11f1-a540-61c3f7fc4e6c.jpg)
Reba McEntire performed Dolly Parton's Appalachian Memories
Actress Sally Field, who starred in Steel Magnolias opposite Dolly Parton, led a tribute to the country music star, who died last month.
Field described Parton as "genuine, humble, supportive and blisteringly funny" as she introduced a special performance by country singer Reba McEntire.
"She was a humanitarian whose contribution has made a profound difference across our country," Field said of Parton, who won an Emmy herself in 2021.
"God bless you Dolly Parton my friend, I am not the only one on Earth who will love you for ever and ever."
Earlier in the night, Field won best actress in a limited series or movie for Remarkably Smart Creatures, a Netflix film about an octopus who observes the staff in his aquarium.
Catherine O'Hara remembered
Macaulay Culkin honours Catherine O'Hara
Macaulay Culkin, Annie Murphy and Dan Levy delivered a poignant tribute to their late Home Alone and Schitt's Creek co-star Catherine O'Hara. Culkin remembered her as "our mom", and "like a good mom, she always showed up when I asked her to".
Referring to the plot of the Home Alone films, he joked: "She may have forgotten me... twice! But we will always remember her."
Noah Kahan then performed Bridge Over Troubled Water during the in memoriam segment, before Jamie Lee Curtis paid an emotional tribute to actor and director Rob Reiner.
Reiner, who died last December, received a posthumous Emmy last week for his guest appearance in The Bear.
Alan Cumming's 'beautiful treachery'
![Alan Cumming accepts the Outstanding Reality Competition Program Award for "The Traitors" onstage during the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards at Peacock Theater on September 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/3e9f/live/28036d20-b0ad-11f1-bc1f-3f186ca4140c.jpg)
Cumming won best reality host for The Traitors during a preliminary Emmys ceremony last week
In other award categories, Scottish TV presenter Alan Cumming accepted the best reality show prize for the US version of The Traitors, an honour he said would encourage the team to "do better and go bigger".
"It is so beautiful that a show about treachery and betrayal brings people together," he joked, as he also thanked his dog Lala, "the perfect co-host".
On an evening otherwise light on political messages, Cumming concluded his speech by encouraging US citizens to register to vote ahead of the midterm elections in November.
Stephen Colbert's swansong
![Stephen Colbert, wins the Outstanding Variety Series Award for âThe Late Show With Stephen Colbertâ poses backstage for the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards at Peacock Theater on September 14, 2026 in Los Angeles, California.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/5578/live/e6717f10-b0ab-11f1-9c5d-0dd6cc52f198.jpg)
Colbert won for his late-night talk show, which ended in May after being cancelled
Stephen Colbert won best variety series after presenting his final episode of The Late Show in May.
The presenter said nightly talk shows were a "fantastic incubator for young people to come in, work professionally, on a deadline, in collaboration, and that is the future of our business that we have to look after".
He added: "I want to say to the audience, thank you so much for watching, we hope you enjoyed the show, we had a great time doing it for you. That's it, thank you, and catch you on the flip."
summary: Welsh actor Matthew Rhys made Emmy Awards history by becoming the first person to win two lead acting prizes in a single night, recognized for his roles in Widow's Bay and The Beast In Me. Other major winners included Jean Smart and Allison Janney, who both equaled the record for the most acting wins ever with eight total victories. The ceremony also featured emotional tributes to late figures including Dolly Parton and Catherine O'Hara, alongside a humanitarian award presented to Michael J Fox.
key_points: Matthew Rhys won best lead actor in a limited series for The Beast In Me and best lead actor in a comedy for Widow's Bay.
Jean Smart and Allison Janney tied the record for the most acting wins ever, each earning their eighth career Emmy.
The Pitt won best drama series, while its lead star Noah Wyle won best lead actor in a drama for the second consecutive year.
Michael J Fox received the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award for his Parkinson's disease advocacy and campaigning.
Tributes were paid during the ceremony to late stars Dolly Parton, Catherine O'Hara, and Rob Reiner.

title: Macklemore dropped from Ed Sheeran tour following Palestine advocacy
author: Tamara Khandaker
content:
![MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - MAY 15: Macklemore performs at Rod Laver Arena on May 15, 2024 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Morgan Hancock/Getty Images)](https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/getty_6aa8378e89-1789409166.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
Billionaire Robert Kraft has confirmed that Macklemore has been barred from Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, after the rapper said his support for Palestine led to his being dropped from pop star Ed Sheeran’s tour.
Kraft said in a statement received by Al Jazeera on Monday that Macklemore’s recent performances and what he described as a “broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery” led Gillette Stadium, which is owned and operated by the Kraft group, to determine that his appearances there on September 25 and 26 “would cross that line”.
