- list 3 of 4Eurovision final marred by protests as five countries boycott over Israel
- list 4 of 4Macklemore defends ‘Free Palestine’ call after Ed Sheeran concert backlash
“This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf,” Kraft said. “But that advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas … whose horrific actions have caused immeasurable suffering for Palestinians and Israelis alike.”
Kraft’s statement came after Macklemore claimed Sheeran informed him that Kraft was barring him from performing at Gillette Stadium. Macklemore also alleged that Kraft had rallied other stadium owners to issue an ultimatum: “If Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues.”
Kraft did not directly address the claim that he had contacted other stadium owners.
Macklemore made the allegations in a lengthy Instagram statement on Monday, the same day promoter Messina Touring Group confirmed that venues had refused to host upcoming shows with the rapper on the lineup.
“I’m not sure how to start this. So I’m going to speak from the heart and share the truth,” Macklemore wrote. “Ed Sheeran and his team have made the decision to remove me from The Loop tour.”
But Macklemore said neither he nor Sheeran, nor singer Pink, who had reposted criticism of his performance, were the victims in the controversy.
Messina Touring Group, the tour promoter, confirmed Macklemore’s removal from the tour in a statement to Rolling Stone magazine on Monday.
“We have been notified by venues on the upcoming US tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans,” the Messina Touring Group said. “After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates.”
Al Jazeera has not independently verified Macklemore’s account, and neither Sheeran nor his press office has commented.
‘I don’t take sides’
Macklemore described Sheeran as a close friend of 13 years and said the two had several difficult conversations over the past week.
“He couldn’t get past his public-facing, ‘I don’t take sides,’” Macklemore wrote, referring to Sheeran’s reluctance to take a public stance on Israel’s war on Gaza.
The controversy began after Macklemore’s performances at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on September 4 and 5, where he repeatedly voiced support for Palestinians and performed Hind’s Hall, his protest song inspired by the pro-Palestinian student movement.
The Israeli American Council later launched a petition calling for Macklemore to be removed from Sheeran’s tour. Pink also reposted criticism of the performance that called for an apology and ticket refunds.
Macklemore argued that performing alongside one of the world’s biggest artists had made his advocacy more threatening to those who opposed it.
“If I kept doing the shows, saying Free Palestine, with Ed implicitly supporting it, the crowd getting loud and showing undeniable support for Palestinian liberation, what artist might speak out next?” he wrote.
He said he hoped the dispute would not end his friendship with Sheeran, but made clear he did not regret speaking out.
“Free Palestine,” he said.
summary: Rapper Macklemore has been removed from Ed Sheeran's tour and barred from Gillette Stadium following his vocal support for Palestine during recent concerts. Billionaire Robert Kraft stated that the venue ban was due to what he described as Macklemore's history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery, rather than his advocacy for Palestinians. The Messina Touring Group confirmed the rapper's removal, noting that multiple venues refused to host shows with Macklemore on the lineup.
key_points: Macklemore was dropped from Ed Sheeran's tour after expressing support for Palestine and performing his protest song 'Hind's Hall' at MetLife Stadium.
Robert Kraft confirmed that Gillette Stadium barred Macklemore, citing a broader history of alleged antisemitic rhetoric and imagery.
The Messina Touring Group stated that various venues refused to host concerts with Macklemore, threatening the cancellation of the tour.
Macklemore alleged that Kraft rallied other stadium owners to issue an ultimatum regarding his appearance on the tour.

title: Macklemore dropped from Ed Sheeran tour after 'free Palestine' speech
author: Gabriela Pomeroy
content:
![Close up of Macklemore, who has shaved blonde hair, and is wearing a blue striped shirt.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/0833/live/c4a7c1f0-b065-11f1-a540-61c3f7fc4e6c.jpg)
- Published
Rapper Macklemore has been dropped from Ed Sheeran's US tour after making pro-Palestinian comments on stage earlier this month.
The artist - whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty - had been the opening act for Sheeran's Loop tour, but was criticised by Jewish groups after saying "Free Palestine" at two concerts and making political speeches.
Macklemore stood by his comments on Monday, confirming that he had been cut from the tour and writing in a statement that the real victims are the Palestinian people in Gaza.
Ed Sheeran has not yet commented, and who will replace Macklemore for the rest of the tour is unknown.
The controversy began on 4 September, when Macklemore, a long-time pro-Palestine activist, performed at Ed Sheeran's concert at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.
He told the audience: "A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so that I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very, very dear to my heart: Free Palestine."
He then performed his song Hind's Hall, which condemns Israel's military action in Gaza, while video footage of the devastation in Gaza was shown on the big screen.
After that performance, the campaign group StopAntisemitism criticised the rapper, saying "Jewish fans bought tickets to see Ed Sheeran sing... not to be ambushed by Macklemore's anti-Israel propaganda."
The next night, Macklemore returned to the same stage and directly addressed his "Jewish brothers and sisters" in the audience.
"Criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide, is in no way a criticism of you," he said, adding that he wanted people in Gaza and the West Bank to know they had not been forgotten.
Israel rejects allegations of genocide. It says its troops conduct self-defence operations in Gaza and the occupied West Bank in accordance with international law.
The Israeli military launched a campaign in Gaza in response to an unprecedented Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 were taken hostage.
During Israel's military campaign in Gaza more than 73,780 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
![Singer/songwriter Ed Sheeran (L) and rapper Macklemore perform during the 2014 iHeartRadio Music Festival at the MGM Grand Garden Arena on September 20, 2014 in Las Vegas, Nevada.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/fec9/live/093de4c0-b066-11f1-b9fd-8be7457ad079.jpg)
Ed Sheeran and Macklemore, pictured in 2014, have been friends for 13 years, the rapper said in his statement
But the backlash against Macklemore only grew louder, and included a petition by the Israeli-American Council urging Sheeran to remove him from the tour.
"This was an Ed Sheeran concert - not a political rally, not a protest, and not an activist event," the council said, adding that the rapper used "biased messaging and disputed claims."
In his statement on Instagram, which was nearly 1,000 words long, Macklemore said that after a week of "difficult conversations" with Sheeran, that ultimately ended "in a place of fundamental disagreement", he was dropped from the lineup.
Tour promoter, Messina Touring Group, told Rolling Stone magazine that it had been told by venues that they would not allow Macklemore to perform, "which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans."
American businessman Robert Kraft, who owns the Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts, said he banned Macklemore because the venue would not "provide a platform for hate speech," accusing the rapper of "a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric".
"I agree with Macklemore, too many lives have been lost and there has been too much suffering, but only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate," Kraft said.
In his statement, Macklemore said he empathised with the difficult position Sheeran was in, but criticised the English singer for not taking a stance.
"Taking a side can cost you. Money, brand deals, sponsorships, festivals, private shows, relationships and access. I've lost all of those things. But there is no neutral position between the oppressor and the oppressed," he wrote.
He also addressed the accusations of antisemitism, writing that "one of the most effective ways to enforce silence has been to weaponize the accusation of antisemitism".
Macklemore added: "When criticizing Israel, opposing Zionism or saying "Free Palestine" gets conflated with hatred of Jewish people, it doesn't protect Jewish people. It protects Israel from accountability."
But he emphasised that even though he only did two shows on the tour, if his words succeeded in "turning the conversation back to Palestine, then it was the most successful tour I've ever been on."
![Pink wearing a black, feathery outfit on a red carpet.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/b28c/live/bb2d4280-b06f-11f1-9819-95a805e73cfa.jpg)
Pink was drawn into the controversy when she reposted criticism of Macklemore
The controversy also saw US singer Pink, who is Jewish, drawn into the furore after she reposted a message criticising Macklemore.
She, too, received massive backlash for her stance, with critics taking aim at everything from her parenting style to past comments about women like Paris Hilton, Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera.
She later posted a long statement saying she does not speak for Israel or for any government, and explained her criticism of Macklemore's comments and conduct on stage.
"Last weekend [Macklemore] stood in front of a stadium full of music-loving families, with violent images from a war on the screens, dedicated a song to the movement of his choice, and then took the mic to tell all of the Jews in the stadium that it wasn't about them."
"You don't get to decide that for us," she wrote.
Pink also pointed out that in 2014, Macklemore performed his same-sex anthem Same Love at the Grammys, while a mass wedding ceremony saw 33 LGBTQ+ couples get married on stage.
But later that year he apologised for a costume he wore which included a black wig, beard and a fake hooked nose, which critics said was antisemitic.
summary: Rapper Macklemore has been removed as the opening act for Ed Sheeran's US tour following backlash over his pro-Palestinian stage speeches and performance of his song "Hind's Hall." Jewish groups and venue operators criticized the rapper for using the concerts to make political statements, leading tour promoters and venues to drop him. Macklemore stood by his comments in a statement, while Ed Sheeran has not publicly commented on the matter.
key_points: Macklemore was dropped from Ed Sheeran's tour after saying "Free Palestine" and performing his song condemning Israel's military action in Gaza at two concerts.
Groups such as StopAntisemitism and the Israeli-American Council criticized the rapper for bringing political protests into music concerts.
Venues and promoters stated that allowing Macklemore to perform could lead to tour cancellations and impact hundreds of thousands of fans.
Macklemore defended his comments in a statement, arguing that criticism of Israel is not criticism of Jewish people, while denying accusations of antisemitism.

title: Oasis announce 2027 tour, including return to Knebworth 30 years after historic concerts
author: Laura Snapes
content:
Oasis have finally confirmed new tour dates for 2027, including their long-rumoured return to Knebworth for a run of shows 30 years after they played a historic two nights at the Hertfordshire venue in 1996.
“Start the celebrations!”, the band said in a statement. “After a period of reflection, The Most Damaging Pop Cultural Force in Recent British History” – a quote from a Guardian opinion piece about the band – “has declared itself fit for purpose and will once again return to lift the spirits of the people. Come witness the fitness. It shall be a sight to behold.”
Titled Oasis Live 27, the dates encompass the UK, Ireland, mainland Europe and the US, beginning in Glasgow on 21 May, and touring through Manchester, Munich, Barcelona, Amsterdam, Paris, Rome, Boston, Las Vegas and Slane Castle (north of Dublin), ending with four nights at Knebworth in September.
The band had teased the news in a massive drone display above Manchester’s Etihad stadium last week, after hinting at the dates on Instagram.
The tour follows Oasis’s acclaimed 2025 reunion, which saw them play 41 dates spanning the UK, Europe, North and South America, east Asia and Australia, 16 years after they split in 2009. “You struggle to think of another artist that’s received such a vociferous reception,” wrote Guardian critic Alexis Petridis in a five-star review of the first night of the tour in Cardiff.
The 2027 tour will be Oasis’s first visit to mainland Europe since their reunion and adds US cities they didn’t visit during that run. Their return to Paris will be particularly poignant, given it was shortly before a 2009 set at the city’s Rock en Seine festival that the band first split up.
In the UK, tickets will cost between £71.50 and £266.60. Those hoping to buy them will have a happier experience than those in the same position last year: all pricing information for Oasis Live 27 has been shared in advance after action by the competition watchdog forced Ticketmaster to change how it advertises tickets, including ending “misleading” information about seats, after fan backlash over its handling of the 2025 tour.
Last year, the use of “tiered” pricing meant that some fans, expecting to pay £148.50 per ticket, found themselves faced with costs of £350 at the checkout – and only a matter of minutes in which to decide whether to go ahead with their purchases. Now, Ticketmaster must tell fans 24 hours in advance if tiered pricing will be used, which tickets it covers and how the system works. When the sale is live, the price range must be shared and updated as tickets sell out.
Anyone wanting a ticket for 2027’s tour must register between now and 4pm BST on 17 September. The registration has been introduced “to reduce queuing times and organised ticket touting in order to give genuine fans the best possible chance to buy tickets,” according to organisers.
![The members of Oasis having a rough-and-tumble embrace in an empty field at Knebworth 1996](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/a1055b1b4574d66d1a551aae2ed6823c66c07917/66_0_3511_2810/master/3511.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Fans had a chance to revisit the 2025 tour – or catch up on what they missed – as a documentary about the reunion, Don’t Look Back in Anger, hit cinemas last week after premiering at the Venice film festival. It earned glowing reviews for its emotional portrait of the band’s fans.
The documentary didn’t touch on the furore around ticket prices, other than one onstage comment from Liam Gallagher: after referring to the people in the cheap seats, he added: “Actually there are no cheap seats, sorry about that.”
The news that Oasis would return to Knebworth was first teased by an unlikely suspect, the British peer Baroness Taylor of Stevenage. In October 2025, she suggested in the House of Lords that Oasis would be playing five shows “in the fantastic venue of Knebworth House”, just a mile away from her own residence.
She quickly retracted her comments in the chamber, clarifying to the Guardian that she was “speaking hypothetically following speculation that they would play Knebworth again as they did in August 1996”.
In August, it was reported that SJM Concerts managing director Simon Moran had secured an events licence for Knebworth, prompting further speculation about an Oasis appearance. The licence would cover audiences of 125,000 people.
At the original 1996 dates, the band played to 250,000 fans – just one tenth of the number who applied for tickets, estimated at the time to be more than 4% of the entire British population. “This is history,” Noel Gallagher told the Knebworth crowd on the second night. The band recently started selling replicas of Noel and Liam’s respective outfits on the night.
A 2021 documentary, the prosaically titled Oasis Knebworth 1996, positioned the concerts as “the peak of British culture” wrote Guardian music editor Ben Beaumont-Thomas in a four-star review. The film’s voiceovers, he continued, implied that “all live music went downhill afterwards. It’s a lie every generation tells itself.” Liam subsequently headlined the park in June 2022.
UK Music estimated that the band’s five nights at Manchester’s Heaton Park last year led to music tourist spending in the north-west rising 16% year on year to £1.4bn. Momentum behind the tour was also credited with boosting the UK’s ongoing vinyl revival.
Oasis are also rumoured to be headlining Glastonbury 2027, the festival’s return after a fallow year in 2026.
Their reunion poured more fuel on the fire of enduring Britpop nostalgia, sparking a critically panned play documenting the rivalry between Oasis and Blur, an album called Britpop by Robbie Williams and even an embrace of Oasis in the US, a country that had been historically immune to their charms.
Oasis Live 27 tour dates in full
Celtic Park, Glasgow: 21, 23, 25, 28, 29 May
Etihad Stadium, Manchester: 4, 6, 8, 11, 12, 15, 18, 19, 22, 25, 26 June
Allianz Arena, Munich: 2, 3 July
Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys, Barcelona: 10, 11 July
Johan Cruijff Arena, Amsterdam: 16, 17 July
Stade de France, Paris: 23, 24 July
Stadio Olimpico, Rome: 29, 30 July
Gillette Stadium, Boston: 10, 13, 14 August
Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas: 20, 21, 24 August
Slane Castle, Ireland: 4, 5 September
Knebworth, Hertfordshire: 11, 12, 18, 19 September
summary: Oasis has announced their Oasis Live 27 tour, which will include dates across the UK, Ireland, mainland Europe, and the US starting in May 2027. The tour features a four-night run at Knebworth in September, marking 30 years since their historic 1996 concerts. Ticket sales will feature stricter transparency rules regarding tiered pricing following fan backlash during their 2025 reunion tour, alongside a mandatory registration system to reduce queuing and ticket touting.
key_points: The Oasis Live 27 tour begins in Glasgow on 21 May 2027 and concludes with four nights at Knebworth in September.
The tour follows the band's acclaimed 2025 reunion tour and will include visits to mainland Europe and US cities not previously visited on that run.
UK tickets will cost between £71.50 and £266.60, with pricing information shared in advance due to regulatory changes forcing Ticketmaster to end misleading advertising.
Fans must register by 4pm BST on 17 September to participate in the ticket sale in order to reduce queuing times and ticket touting.

title: Oasis tour announcement live: Noel and Liam expected to unveil 2027 dates today
author: Roisin O'Connor
content:
Oasis are widely expected to be announcing a new tour today, with fans poised for 4pm BST when the band will be sharing their news.
The Manchester rock legends teased the announcement last week with a spectacular drone display in Manchester, with the band’s logo showing up in lights along with the date 14/09/26 and the time 4pm BST.
Oasis have also been dropping hints about potential tour venues over the past few weeks on their social media channels, including the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, Celtic Park in Glasgow, and Knebworth in Hertfordshire.
Even before the band’s 2025 reunion concerts had concluded, fans and the media were speculating that once-warring brothers Noel and Liam Gallagher would be back on stage together again in the near future, such was the success of last year’s tour.
The announcement comes a week after Noel and Liam attended the UK premiere of the documentary film Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger from Steven Knight and co-directors Dylan Southern and Will Lovelace, showing behind-the-scenes footage and concert clips from the 2025 reunion.
Tickets to the Oasis Live ‘25 shows sold out within minutes of going on sale, with the tour estimated by Forbes to have generated over $400m (£293m) in revenue, and Noel and Liam each pocketing between $50m-$100m. As a result, the pair cracked the Sunday Times Rich List this year with a combined net worth of $375m.
Follow for the latest updates on today’s 4pm announcement.
The biggest revelations from Oasis film Don’t Look Back in Anger
As Oasis prepare to make their announcement, here are the biggest things we learned from their new tour documentary, Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger.
How Liam and Noel reflected on their feud
We all saw them trading insults in the press and on social media (Liam comparing Noel to a potato is the stuff of legend, while Noel famously described Liam as “the angriest man you’ll ever meet. He’s like a man with a fork in a world of soup.”), but how did they feel about the moment Oasis broke up?
“It didn’t sit right with me,” Noel says in new Oasis documentary Don’t Look Back in Anger, even while describing Liam as a “f***ing pain in the arse”.
Liam refers to the row that brought everything crashing down in 2009 as “a little argument” – Noel has said previously that Liam came into his dressing room wielding a guitar “like an axe” and nearly took his face off with it. Potato, potato.
Don’t Look Back in Anger does what its title suggests, and skirts around the gory details of the brothers’ animosity. Instead, we hear Noel confess that he was born with “one fatal flaw – I can’t forgive people”.
He and Liam also agree that after the split, “everything felt f***ing weird”; Noel saw the world become “a s*** f***ing place – people want escape”. And that’s what the reunion was going to give them.
How Noel Gallagher felt about the 2025 Oasis reunion
Noel has a reputation as a grouch – Don’t Look Back in Anger does a lot to dispel that. For the first 40 minutes onstage in Cardiff he’s fighting back tears, overwhelmed by the reaction from the 80,000-strong crowd. “I wasn’t prepared for the intense outpouring… the sense of what it meant to people,” he says. He sees fathers with their sons in the crowd and has to fight not to bawl, seeing how the band’s music has been passed on to younger generations.
VIDEO: Oasis tease time and date for major announcement
How Noel and Liam Gallagher's relationship is today
One of my favourite revelations from the new Oasis documentary, Don’t Look Back in Anger, is what Noel and Liam’s relationship is like today - in Noel’s view, it’s better than it’s ever been.
In the documentary, Noel says there are “two Liams” – the serious guy he saw in rehearsals, and the one onstage balancing a tambourine on his head and making it look cool: “If I did that, I’d look like an utter c***.”
Halfway through the documentary we finally see them sitting next to one another in the present day: Liam makes Noel howl with laughter as he talks about the genius behind their habit of barely moving in live shows. “Imagine Mick Jagger… if there’s one night where he’s just like, ‘Ah I can’t be f***ed,’ but he’s got to,” Liam explains. “Us standing still onstage… genius.”
Noel says he feels like patching things up “fixed the narrative” of the band. They text one another regularly – “we never did that before” – and send each other silly videos. The Oasis story is no longer about the anger between brothers. As Noel puts it: “Now it's about forgiveness.”
Rock ‘n’ Roll, flying pints and a brotherly hug: Inside Oasis’s first reunion show
I was also lucky enough to be there at the first Oasis reunion show in Cardiff, Wales, on 4 July 2025. Here’s my report from the night:
![](https://static.the-independent.com/2025/07/04/21/40/IMG_2085.jpg?trim=570,97,2552,371&width=1200&height=800&crop=1200:800)
VIDEO: Oasis perform 'Acquiesce' on opening night of reunion tour
Review: In Cardiff, Oasis deliver the rock reunion to end them all
It was an emotional one at the first Oasis Live ‘25 show in Cardiff, Wales, on 4 July 2025 - our critic Mark Beaumont did a brilliant job of summing up the jubilant atmosphere in his five-star review.
![](https://static.the-independent.com/2025/07/05/0/10/Britain-Oasis-Concert-xpjtnsn7.jpeg?trim=1,0,1,0&width=1200&height=800&crop=1200:800)
Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger review – The energy from the reunion shows is like atoms fusing
Our critic Phil Harrison was impressed after attending the UK premiere of Steven Knight’s new film, the documentary Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger.
You can read his four-star review here:
![](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/09/08/11/01M1ZSERVXZNVRDEE8QN98WMDW.jpg?trim=46,0,46,0&width=1200&height=800&crop=1200:800)
summary: Rock band Oasis are widely expected to announce new tour dates following teasers on social media and a drone display in Manchester. The announcement follows the massive success of their 2025 reunion tour and the release of a new documentary, Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger. Noel and Liam Gallagher have stated that their relationship is currently better than ever, noting that patching things up has changed the band's narrative to one of forgiveness.
key_points: Oasis teased a major announcement for 4pm BST following a drone display and social media venue hints.
The band's 2025 reunion tour generated over $400 million in revenue and sold out within minutes.
A new documentary titled Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger covers behind-the-scenes footage and reflections on the brothers' past feud.
Noel Gallagher stated that his relationship with Liam is better than ever and they now text regularly.

title: Emmy Awards 2026: What to expect from the ceremony and how to watch
author: Steven McIntosh
content:
![Zendaya attends the Los Angeles premiere of HBO's Euphoria season three - she is wearing a black halterneck dress and hoop earrings](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/ee34/live/754b5420-8b33-11f1-b170-2de1c3aec73b.jpg)
Zendaya is the only Euphoria star to be nominated for an acting award
- Published
Beef, Hacks, Pluribus and The Pitt are a few of the TV shows nominated at this year's Emmy Awards, which take place on Monday in Los Angeles.
Widow's Bay, DTF St Louis, Slow Horses, The Bear and Abbott Elementary are also competing for prizes at the ceremony, which is seen as the US television industry's most prestigious event.
Actors nominated for trophies include Zendaya, Noah Wyle, Sarah Snook and Colman Domingo, while Matthew Rhys, Carey Mulligan and Jack Lowden are among the British nominees.
But several big shows are not represented - viral sensation Heated Rivalry is not eligible for the Emmys, while there is a weaker presence for the final series of Euphoria and Stranger Things.
Here's everything you need to know about this year's Emmy Awards.
Which TV shows are the frontrunners?
![Noah Wyle at The Pitt Los Angeles premiere, wearing a brown suit and beige shirt and tie](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/0807/live/25f22c20-8ffa-11f1-b8ee-9b3c26ad07bb.jpg)
Noah Wyle is nominated for best drama actor for his performance in medical series The Pitt
The Emmys split their nominations into three overarching categories: comedy, drama and limited or anthology series.
Best drama is generally seen as the night's most prestigious prize, and last year's winner The Pitt is back to defend its title following its second series.
The acclaimed medical drama also has eight individual acting nominations, including one for its star, Noah Wyle.
Other dramas nominated include Pluribus, Slow Horses, The Diplomat and Game of Thrones prequel A Knight Of The Seven Kingdoms.
Over in the comedy categories, Hollywood satire Hacks is predicted by many to continue its hugely successful Emmys streak following its fifth and final season.
The show's expected wins could include acting prizes for its two stars, Jean Smart and Hannah Einbinder.
![Hannah Einbinder and Jean Smart, winners of outstanding supporting actress in a comedy Series and lead actress in a comedy series for Hacks at last year's Emmys - Einbinder is wearing an off-the-shoulder silver and black dress, while Smart is wearing a forest green high-necked dress](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/a6e9/live/1ceff380-9010-11f1-aabc-c3c7aa714117.jpg)
Hannah Einbinder and Jean Smart could repeat their previous Emmy wins following the final season of Hacks
Smart already has four Emmys for Hacks, having never lost for her performances in the previous four seasons. Another win would bring her total Emmy tally to eight, tying the record held by Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Cloris Leachman.
Possible challengers in the comedy categories include Widow's Bay, Shrinking, Abbott Elementary and Nobody Wants This.
Elsewhere, the second season of Netflix's Beef could be a strong contender in the limited or anthology series category, and win acting prizes for its stars Carey Mulligan and Oscar Isaac.
But it faces strong competition from shows such as All Her Fault, The Beast in Me and DTF St Louis, which had a particularly strong showing at last week's Creative Arts Emmys.
British nominees alongside Mulligan include Riz Ahmed (Bait), Rufus Sewell (The Diplomat), Kate OâFlynn (Widowâs Bay) and Gary Oldman and Jack Lowden (both for Slow Horses).
And many are keeping a particularly close eye on Welsh star Matthew Rhys, who is nominated in two different lead actor categories - for comedy Widow's Bay and limited series The Beast in Me.
Why isn't Heated Rivalry nominated?
![Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams attend the 2026 Vanity Fair Oscar party in LA, they are both wearing sheer chiffon black tops.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/4050/live/f163cc20-900d-11f1-aabc-c3c7aa714117.jpg)
Heated Rivalry, starring Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams, does not qualify for the Emmys
The buzziest show of the last year, Heated Rivalry, starring Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams, is missing from this year's Emmy nominations.
The ice hockey romance did not qualify because it is a fully financed Canadian production, without the US involvement needed to be recognised at the Emmys.
Its ineligibility puzzled many who remember Schitt's Creek, a show more Canadian than maple cream cookies, dominating the Emmys in 2021.
But that qualified because of its financial and broadcast partnerships in the US, including creator and star Dan Levy's own American-based production company.
Heated Rivalry will instead be eligible to compete for the next International Emmys, which take place in New York in November.
Meanwhile, two other viral shows popular with younger audiences that were eligible for the US ceremony had a weaker-than-expected showing in the nominations list.
The final series of Stranger Things is absent in the top categories this year, scoring only seven nominations in technical categories.
And despite its star-packed cast, Euphoria's last season managed only one acting nomination for former winner Zendaya.
What changes have been made to the ceremony?
![Janelle James and Quinta Brunson speak onstage at the 29th Actors Guild Awards in LA in February - James is wearing a black lace dress, Brunson is wearing a white corset top](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/445a/live/ea182fb0-923d-11f1-b2ab-0dd01740f9f6.jpg)
Abbott Elementary stars Janelle James and Quinta Brunson are nominated for comedy acting categories
Two categories have been merged this year - best talk series and best scripted variety series are now combined in a single category: outstanding variety series.
That means chat show hosts such as Jimmy Kimmel will compete against topical variety shows such as Saturday Night Live and Last Week Tonight With John Oliver.
Some other categories were also moved out of the telecast this year and have already been handed out, in an effort to revitalise the ceremony and leave more time for entertainment.
For example, best supporting actor and actress in a limited series, usually awarded during the main ceremony, were moved to the earlier Creative Arts Emmys ceremonies this year.
The total number of trophies awarded on the big night has been reduced from 26 to 19, a move the Academy said was intended to leave room for more musical performances, comedic sketches and unexpected acceptance speeches.
How to watch the Emmy Awards
![Oscar Isaac, wearing a red shirt, and Carey Mulligan, waring a gold sequinned dress, attend the Los Angeles premiere of Netflix's Beef season two in Los Angeles](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/aeb3/live/90471070-8ff2-11f1-b8ee-9b3c26ad07bb.jpg)
Oscar Isaac and Carey Mulligan are nominated for their roles in the second season of Beef
The ceremony will begin at 17:00 PT / 20:00 ET on Monday, taking place at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.
US viewers can watch the Emmy Awards live on NBC or on streaming service Peacock.
In the UK, it will start at 01:00 BST on Tuesday morning, but no British broadcaster is scheduled to show it live.
However, there will be overnight coverage on the BBC News website throughout the red carpet and ceremony.
Who has already won?
![US actress Linda Cardellini, wearing an orange dress, and US actor David Harbour, in a black suit, pose with their Emmys for outstanding supporting actress and actor in a limited or anthology series or movie for DTF St. Louis.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/dbf8/live/24c84440-ac58-11f1-bc1f-3f186ca4140c.jpg)
Linda Cardellini and David Harbour won Emmys last week for their roles in DTF St Louis
Winners at last weekend's Creative Arts Emmys included DTF St Louis stars Linda Cardellini and David Harbour, who won best supporting actress and actor in a limited series.
Betty Gilpin (Widow's Bay), Ernest Harden Jr (The Pitt), Shailene Woodley (Paradise) and the late Rob Reiner (The Bear) all won prizes for their guest acting roles, while British star Julie Andrews won best voiceover performance for Bridgerton.
Other British winners included Alan Cumming, who won best reality host for the US version of The Traitors.
Remarkably Bright Creatures, a drama starring Sally Field and Lewis Pullman about a perceptive octopus who observes the staff in his aquarium, won best movie.
South Park won best animated series, Mr. Scorsese took best docuseries, Love on the Spectrum won best unstructured reality programme, and the Super Bowl Halftime Show Starring Bad Bunny won best variety special.
Who is hosting the ceremony?
![Mariska Hargitay is seen at the Today show in New York in May, she is wearing a white shirt and bronze trousers and is holding a huge blue umbrella](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/1975/live/8cb8a570-8fe5-11f1-9b57-e74b317a0f23.jpg)
Mariska Hargitay is best known for starring in Law & Order: Special Victims Unit
US actress Mariska Hargitay, star of Law and Order: Special Victims Unit, will host this year's Primetime Emmys ceremony.
Her hugely successful crime series, known as SVU, has been running since 1999, and continues to be popular with younger audiences who have discovered it on streaming services.
Hargitay has been Emmy nominated eight times herself for playing detective Olivia Benson, winning for lead actress in a drama series in 2006.
SVU is one of the longest-running TV dramas of all time and is set to reach its 600th episode when its 28th season airs this autumn.
And at last weekend's Creative Arts Emmys, Hargitay also won two prizes for her documentary My Mom Jayne, about her actress mother Jayne Mansfield, who died in a car accident when Hargitay was three.
"Bringing important stories into the light has been the heartbeat of my career," Hargitay said in a statement.
"It's my great honour to host the 78th Emmy Awards and celebrate this extraordinary community of storytellers.
"Whether it's an actor or a director, a costumer or a sound designer, we are all so privileged to take part in creating television that unites us."
summary: The 2026 Emmy Awards ceremony takes place in Los Angeles on Monday, featuring frontrunners like The Pitt, Hacks, and Beef. This year's event introduces format changes, such as reducing the number of trophies handed out during the main telecast and combining talk and variety series into a single category. Meanwhile, viral sensation Heated Rivalry missed out on nominations due to lacking the necessary US financial involvement, and Law & Order star Mariska Hargitay is set to host the ceremony.
key_points: The Primetime Emmys ceremony will be hosted by Mariska Hargitay in Los Angeles on Monday.
Top nominated shows include The Pitt, Hacks, Beef, and Slow Horses.
Heated Rivalry did not qualify for the Emmys because it is a fully financed Canadian production without required US backing.
The Academy reduced the number of trophies awarded during the main broadcast from 26 to 19 to allow more room for entertainment and sketches.
Creative Arts Emmy winners included Linda Cardellini, David Harbour, and Julie Andrews.

title: SNL UK kicks off second series with Harry and Meghan sketch: ‘Daddy, I’m home’
author: Isobel Lewis
content:
Saturday Night Live UK returned to our screens with a sharp opening sketch targeting the Duke and Duchess of Sussex and their move back to the UK.
Saturday (12 September) evening’s broadcast began with a topical cold open starring Jack Shep and Ayoade Bamgboye as Prince Harry and Meghan Markle for the first time.
The couple were seen on a trip to Balmoral to visit the King and Queen Camilla (Larry Dean and Emma Sidi, reprising performances from the first series) following their return to the UK after six years in America.
The sketch kicked off with Harry and Meghan entering Balmoral Castle upon their recent resettlement on Harry’s home soil, with the former exclaiming: “Daddy, I’m home!”
![From L-R: Bamgboye, Shep, Dean and Sidi in the series two opener](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/09/13/10/47/Screenshot-2026-09-13-at-11-25-22.png)
Poking fun at their status as non-working royals, Charles told them that the castle is for “royals only”, while Camilla welcomed Meghan by calling her “as brown as ever”.
A dig was also made at Meghan’s lifestyle empire by way of her Netflix series With Love, Meghan, as the former Suits star insisted she is a “whizz in the kitchen” only to present Camilla with a block of ice as a gift.
“It’s true, she hires the best cooks,” Harry quipped.
After the couple shared their plans to move back to the UK, Charles said: “Don’t tell me you spent all your Netflix money already?”
![The real Meghan and Harry have recently relocated to the UK](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/09/08/11/4aff701cc04eb292f2ea0b322c059f63Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg4OTQzNDkx-2.83618974.jpg)
“Daddy, it was $60 million,” Harry whiningly responded. “How long was it meant to last? I’m not asking for much.”
As Harry explained that he “doesn’t want to be a regular guy”, Andy Burnham, played by cast member George Fouracres, appeared on the scene.
“Did somebody say ‘regular guy’? I’m the new PM and I’m nothing like the last one,” he said, in reference to Fouracres having also played then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer on the first series of SNL UK.
Several jokes were made about Burnham, who became Prime Minister in July, with the sketch ending with an inspiring speech in which he said: “Like Gary Barlow before me, I’m just a regular man from the north with a dream, a relatable manner and a massive son.”
![Shep and Bamgboye played the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for the first time](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/09/13/9/36/Screenshot-2026-09-13-at-09-57-20.png)
Harry and Meghan then decided to be “regular” like Mr Burnham, and the skit closed before leading into a musical number performed by this week’s host, Wicked star Jeff Goldblum. Irish singer CMAT served as the musical guest later in the episode.
The British sketch spin-off returned this weekend with all 11 original cast members still involved, while Such Brave Girls star Freddie Meredith has also joined the troupe of comedy actors.
In his three-star review of the series two opener, The Independent’s Nick Hilton wrote: “SNL sketches are always spotty, and this season opener is more miss than hit.”
The show continues next weekend with Jamie Demetriou to front episode two (19 September) and Amelia Dimoldenberg hosting the following week (26 September).
summary: Saturday Night Live UK kicked off its second series with a cold open sketch featuring the Duke and Duchess of Sussex visiting Balmoral Castle after moving back to the UK. The satirical sketch targeted the couple's non-working royal status, their Netflix deal, and lifestyle brand, while also introducing a new segment featuring Prime Minister Andy Burnham. The episode was hosted by Jeff Goldblum with musical guest CMAT.
key_points: Saturday Night Live UK returned for its second series with a cold open featuring Prince Harry and Meghan Markle.
The sketch mocked the couple's return to the UK after six years in America and their status as non-working royals.
Cast member George Fouracres appeared as the new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham.
The season opener was hosted by Jeff Goldblum, with CMAT serving as the musical guest.

title: ‘SNL U.K.’ Mocks Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s British Return in Cold Open: ‘Don’t Tell Me You’ve Spent All Your Netflix Money Already!’
author: Scott Bryan
content:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s recent much-publicized return to England was mocked in the cold open of the first episode of “Saturday Night Live U.K.” Season 2.
The cold open began with Larry Dean as King Charles II and Emma Sidi as Queen Camilla relaxing at Balmoral Castle in Scotland (“I do love our weekends away. No responsibilities, just like every other day,” says Camilla.)
They are then interrupted by the arrival of Harry (Jack Shep) and Meghan (Ayoade Bamgboye). With much of the skit consisting of them being in a close embrace — to the disgust of King Charles — there were countless one-liners making fun of their decision to return to the U.K.
“What do you two want?” asked an infuriated Charles. “Don’t tell me you’ve spent that Netflix money already.”
Popular on Variety
“Daddy, it was $16 million,” replied Harry. “How long was it supposed to last?”
“What a waste you’ve become, you’re lucky your father is not around to see this,” Charles responded, a line which received a large reaction in the room.
Meghan’s lifestyle brands were also riffed on, with her presenting an ice tray to Camilla. “I made it myself,” she said. “I can give you the recipe. I’m a whizz in the kitchen.”
“She hires the best chefs,” Harry added.
George Fouracres, who received acclaim for his acute portrayal of former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, also made his first appearance as Prime Minister Andy Burnham, wearing his trademark black rimmed glasses.
“I’m the new PM. And I’m nothing like the last one,” he said. Making fun of Burnham’s raft of policies over the summer and his attempts at being relatable despite being in high office, the skit ended up with him saying: “I will buy everybody a pint, because I want you to like me. I need you to like me.”
The first episode of “SNL U.K.” was hosted by Jeff Goldblum, who performed a jazzy number about spending time in London during his monologue.
summary: The second season premiere of "Saturday Night Live U.K." opened with a skit mocking Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's recent return to England. The cold open featured parodies of King Charles, Queen Camilla, Harry, and Meghan, joking about their finances and lifestyle brands. The episode also featured George Fouracres as Prime Minister Andy Burnham and was hosted by Jeff Goldblum.
key_points: "Saturday Night Live U.K." Season 2 opened with a cold open mocking Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's return to England.
The sketch featured parodies of King Charles and Queen Camilla interacting with Harry and Meghan at Balmoral Castle.
Jokes were made regarding Harry and Meghan's Netflix deal and her lifestyle brands.
George Fouracres appeared as Prime Minister Andy Burnham in the episode.
The season premiere was hosted by Jeff Goldblum.

title: Latest On Willow Nightingale's Status (AEW News)
author: Andrew Pollard
content:
![Willow Nightingale](https://d2thvodm3xyo6j.cloudfront.net/media/2026/07/9f794fbf872d2a89ffd242021a6ca2ac.jpg) 
Having suffered a legitimate broken hand injury in the build to AEW All In last month, there's now an update on Willow Nightingale's status.
Per Fightful Select, Willow is expected to remain on TV while she recovers from this injury, and this is something that's been the plan from the moment the now-former AEW Women's Champion suffered this injury.
This report also comes on the heels of Nightingale appearing on this past week's Dynamite, where she shared a segment with Thekla and Mercedes Mone, with many expecting to eventually get a triple threat bout between those three.
Of course, as alluded to, Willow Nightingale lost the AEW Women's Title to Mercedes at All In, with that reign clocking in at a relatively brief 35 days. Prior to that, Willow defeated Thekla for that particular piece of gold at AEW Redemption back in July, though Nightingale would only have one successful title defence - beating Maya World on Collision the week before All In - before losing the belt to the CEO.
Up next for AEW, it's All Out on Sunday, September 27th, and it remains to be seen whether we'll get some variation of Mercedes vs. Willow vs. Thekla at that PPV. While she's clearly still recovering from her broken hand, that didn't stop Willow Nightingale from putting in a heck of a performance against Mercedes at All In; a hard-hitting belter of a match that was likely only topped at All In by the phenomenal main event from Will Ospreay and Kenny Omega.
summary: Former AEW Women's Champion Willow Nightingale suffered a legitimate broken hand injury in the build to AEW All In, where she lost her title to Mercedes Mone. Despite the injury, plans from the outset have been for Nightingale to remain on television during her recovery. She recently appeared on Dynamite in a segment with Thekla and Mercedes Mone, fueling speculation about a future triple threat match.
