Nightingale is expected to continue appearing on AEW television while recovering from her injury.
She recently shared a segment with Thekla and Mercedes Mone on Dynamite, hinting at a potential triple threat match.
Nightingale's recent AEW Women's Championship reign lasted 35 days before losing the belt to Mercedes Mone at All In.

title: Céline Dion review – singer’s first live show in years marks a triumphant, emotional return
author: Alim Kheraj
content:
In 2022, when Céline Dion shared that she had been diagnosed with a rare incurable neurological disorder called stiff person syndrome (SPS), there was no guarantee that the 58-year-old would ever tour again. Her condition, which resulted in muscle spasms so strong that it left her with broken ribs, had made it impossible to perform, and in a 2024 documentary, I Am: Céline Dion, fans saw how the disease had constricted her once seemingly infallible voice. Through it all, though, Dion was resolute that she would one day return to the stage. “If I can’t run, I’ll walk. If I can’t walk, I’ll crawl,” she said in the film. “But I won’t stop.”
Thankfully at the opening night of her sold out five-week residency in Paris, her first full-length concerts in six years, no crawling is needed: Céline Dion is back. She glides on to the stage in a black dress, an enormous diamond necklace clasped around her throat, and launches into On ne change pas. There are tears almost immediately: she struggles through the second verse, her voice cracking as she begins to cry. By the time the strum of Destin has kicked in, though, that emotion is replaced with sheer elation. “I made a promise to be back on stage. Singing for you. Singing for me,” she says. “Singing for life.”
![Dion performs during her first concert of a series at the Plenitude Arena in Nanterre, west of Paris on 12 September.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/ae2be4b9a0bccf4e6a96a6416185574719012583/0_0_4506_3004/master/4506.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
That she does. There is no cure for SPS, but the work Dion has put into managing her condition so she can perform again is astounding. Still, clearly some necessary allowances have been made. Some songs such as Because You Loved Me, The Power of Love and My Heart Will Go On have all been transposed down. It’s understandable given the effect her condition has had on her voice, although, in the case of Because You Loved Me and It’s All Coming Back To Me Now, it does somewhat dampen their melodramatic potency.
That is not to say that Dion’s voice is weakened: when she needs to, as she does on the driving Tout l’or des hommes, she can still belt out a note. There’s also some welcome texture to her vocal, too: recently released ballad Dansons sees her embracing her lower register, while Courage, recorded following the death of her late husband René Angélil, is genuinely affecting as Dion allows her voice to get fragile and raspy.
For some, Dion’s success – she has sold more than 200m records and is the third most successful female artist of all time – is inexplicable: to them, her music is the apotheosis of saccharin and anodyne adult contemporary. But for the 30,000-plus in the crowd tonight, that contempt is decidedly absent. After all, you don’t attend a Céline Dion show expecting anything avant garde. You’re there to hear Beauty and the Beast, an unexpected highlight.
![Dion wipes away tears at her first comeback show.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/cb4a3ecf12112cef5ce0a2e8fb83727ee4e2267e/0_0_3678_2940/master/3678.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Still, Dion does have some surprises up her sleeve: the run of J’irai où tu iras, Ne bouge pas and Dans un autre monde provides some rollicking respite from the balladry, Dion strutting up and down the stage while doing vocal acrobatics or fake boxing with backing singer. This is followed by an outlandishly camp disco section, complete with covers of Donna Summer’s I Feel Love (oddly enough, Moroder’s sequenced synths really are a great match), Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This) and a chandelier that quickly morphs into a glitter ball. As Dion shimmies about, separating the covers with a souped-up electronic take on That’s The Way It Is, a sly smile reveals that she, too, knows how ridiculous it all is.
Most astonishing, though, is a rendition of Ebben? Ne andrò lontana from Alfredo Catalani’s opera La Wally: wearing a pink feathered coat and standing a protruding rock that has just emerged from below the stage, Dion pays homage to Maria Callas as fake snow falls from the ceiling on to the audience below. It is brilliant and ludicrous and purists will loathe it. Nevertheless, the kookiness all feels very Céline.
The biggest response from the crowd, many of whom have likely been out practising at one of the many mass karaoke events celebrating Dion’s music throughout Paris this week, arrives during Pour que tu m’aimes encore. The singing is so loud it almost drowns Dion out. It is All By Myself, however, that seems like the most significant for Dion. As the piano solo and slide guitar gives way, she glances upwards before unleashing herself on that final chorus. When she realises she hit the big notes, it’s relief – then triumph – that spreads across her face. Given where she has come from, and her performance on stage tonight, it’s a feeling that is clearly well deserved.
summary: Céline Dion made a triumphant return to the stage at the opening night of her sold-out five-week residency in Paris, marking her first full-length concerts in six years. Diagnosed with stiff person syndrome in 2022, the singer overcame severe muscle spasms and vocal challenges to deliver an emotional and energetic performance. Despite transposing some songs down to accommodate her condition, Dion showcased her vocal strength, embraced new textures, and delighted fans with classic ballads, covers, and operatic homages.
key_points: Céline Dion returned to live performing after six years following her diagnosis with stiff person syndrome in 2022.
The opening night of her Paris residency featured emotional moments, including tears during the opening song and relief after hitting high notes on All By Myself.
Certain well-known songs were transposed down to manage the effects of her condition on her voice.
The setlist included energetic numbers, a disco section, and an operatic homage to Maria Callas.

title: Critics celebrate CÃ©line Dion's 'risky' comeback show in Paris
author: Grace Eliza Goodwin
content:
![Dion dancing in a black dress, holding a microphone, while musicians play behind her](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/7767/live/2b484690-aefa-11f1-a52c-d92eb1a832de.jpg)
- Published
Iconic Canadian pop singer CÃ©line Dion has kicked off her long-awaited comeback show in Paris on Saturday, after a six-year hiatus due to health issues.
The 58-year-old superstar was diagnosed with a rare neurological disorder called stiff person syndrome in 2022, which forced her to pull back from touring.
Dion, one of the best-selling musical artists of all time, has not performed a full show since a 2020 concert in New Jersey - the last before the Covid pandemic cut her tour short. In 2024, she performed just one song at the Paris Olympics closing ceremony.
Saturday marked the first of Dion's 26-show residency at the Paris La DÃ©fense Arena, Europe's largest covered concert arena.
'She's back': Fans dance, sing and cry after CÃ©line Dion's comeback concert in Paris
"I made a promise," she told the Paris audience of about 30,000 people in her emotional return.
"I made a promise to come back, to be back on stage. And here I am. Singing for you, and singing for me," she said.
"I am everything I am because you loved me," she told the crowd.
She also broke down in tears after finishing a song, telling the audience: "I had promised myself not to cry."
"But I'm so happy to see you all. I missed you."
They weren't the only tears of the night, as the star appeared to be overcome with emotion several times.
Dion will be performing in Paris throughout September and October and into the New Year.
The Mirror's Lucy Needham, external noted that the singer was 50 minutes late to start, and may have needed extra time to "compose herself" for the "emotionally charged return".
"Eyes-brimming, the veteran singer gave herself little nods of approval after every line, before finally breaking down at the end of the track, seemingly overwhelmed at having made it through."
After beginning her set in a black gown, she later changed into a trouser suit "to show off some of those signature kooky dance moves," says Needham, adding that she appeared "to be having the time of her life, gyrating and slapping her thighs with glee".
The night was a "a tense, tearful, joyous affair probably even more so for the singer than for her loyal audience," writes The Telegraph's Neil McCormick, external.
She started out slow, he says. "Her voice sounded fragile and exposed, but at least it was her distinctive voice, not some autotuned approximation."
"At first, she was clearly struggling to hold herself together," he continues. "Her vocals wobbled dangerously, as if about to crack or collapse. But she was gaining confidence with every moment back on stage."
She broke down in tears as the audience roared in approval after the first song, and addressed the crowd in both French and English during the set.
"This was a high-stakes, high-wire return, perhaps the riskiest comeback in the history of showbusiness," McCormick continues, referring to her health condition.
But he concludes: "I honestly think I prefer this less superhuman CÃ©line. Her voice is still great, but a bit more raw and real, with a rougher tone, less smoothness in the runs and more edge to her whoops and shrieks."
![Dion wipes away a tear on stage](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/922/cpsprodpb/3b10/live/57183fa0-aefa-11f1-a52c-d92eb1a832de.jpg)
Sarah Leavitt, reporting from Paris for the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC), external, said the crowd "was left without words" by the stunning performance.
She noted that she didn't want to cry, but "of course she cried right away."
Dion also "endeared herself" to the crowd by saying during one song that she wanted to stop and start over.
Will Hodgkinson at the Times of London, external writes in his review, "miraculously, her art will go on," that the performance was "overwhelming".
She "looked suitably humbled and tearful" as she emerged, he said, going on to praise the stage direction.
"Truly, she was throwing the love at the crowd, who threw it right back at her. There was no holding back. It was quite overwhelming, actually," he writes.
The performance was "complete with both costume, key change and air of tragic, important romance".
"CÃ©line Dion's strength lies in being a diva with the common touch while being as French as they get, even if she is Canadian. She fulfilled that role with all the verve you could hope for," writes Hodgkinson.
"The concert had a spiritual feel, with visual interludes steeped in biblical imagery alluding to a pilgrimage," Elsa Keslassy writes for Variety., external
In video clips, Dion is seen wandering in a desert. "The set design was highly cinematic, with a monumental staircase sweeping up one side and a moon dominating the stage, while the backdrop appeared to have a stark, almost brutalist gray texture."
The star, known for power ballads like My Heart Will Go On and Because You Loved Me, has said she will not let her diagnosis control her life.
"The way I see it, I have two choices. Either I train like an athlete and work super hard, or I switch off and it's over," she told French Vogue magazine, external in 2024.
"I've chosen to work with all my body and soul, from head to toe, with a medical team."
Watch: CÃ©line Dion duets with young fan ahead of comeback concert
When Dion announced the first leg of her Paris residency back in March, nine million fans signed up for early access tickets to the concerts, French outlet FRI reported.
The shows sold out so fast that her management company soon announced an additional 10 shows scheduled for May 2027, which have also since sold out.
Fans who were unable to snag tickets to one of the highly anticipated shows have not been left out entirely - events honouring Dion's comeback have dominated Paris in recent weeks.
CÃ©line Dion tribute boat cruises on Seine - complete with costume contests, sing-alongs, DJ sets, are happening throughout September.
Ahead of Saturday's show, fans gathered outside Dion's Paris hotel, LeRoyal Monceau, as early as 06:00 local time to catch a glimpse of the star.
Paris City Hall organised a massive karaoke event on Friday night, attended by thousands, to celebrate Dion's return to the stage.
"I couldn't get tickets to the concert. I'm still keeping my fingers crossed and hoping, but I thought to myself: at least I can share a moment here with all the fans," Rania, a participant at the event, told Reuters.
Earlier this week, thousands of fans also gathered at a historic theatre in central Paris for two nights of karaoke and activities inspired by Dion's music.
And Paris venues and night clubs are hosting Dion-themed events around the city on Saturday night for fans who couldn't get tickets to the actual show.
![A poster with Dion's face near a crowd in Paris](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/b680/live/4614a090-aefa-11f1-a52c-d92eb1a832de.jpg)
![The singer meets fans outside her hotel, with one giving her flowers](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/a5fa/live/a2ca25d0-aefa-11f1-a52c-d92eb1a832de.jpg)
summary: Céline Dion made a triumphant and emotional return to the stage in Paris, kicking off a 26-show residency at the Paris La Défense Arena after a six-year hiatus caused by stiff person syndrome. Critics and fans praised the high-stakes comeback performance, during which the singer delivered a raw and powerful vocal performance despite initial vulnerability. The city of Paris has celebrated her return with tribute events, karaoke gatherings, and sold-out ticket demand.
key_points: Céline Dion returned to the stage in Paris on Saturday for her first full concert since 2020, following a hiatus due to her diagnosis of stiff person syndrome.
The performance marked the beginning of a 26-show residency at the Paris La Défense Arena.
Reviewers described the concert as a high-stakes, emotional, and triumphant event where the singer overcame early vocal fragility to deliver a powerful performance.
Tickets for the residency sold out rapidly, prompting her management to schedule additional shows extending into 2027.
Fans across Paris celebrated her comeback through city-organized karaoke events, themed boat cruises, and gatherings outside her hotel.

title: Woman Unknown wins Venice film festival as NAZA takes special jury prize
author: Philip Oltermann
content:
May el-Toukhy’s Woman Unknown has scooped the Golden Lion at the Venice film festival, at an awards ceremony that also saw the Gaza documentary NAZA win the jury prize.
Set in the immediate aftermath of Danish liberation from Nazi occupation, the Egyptian-Danish director’s film tells the story of a young housemaid, Marie (Mathilde Arcel), who is about to marry her widowed employer but anxious about him discovering a shameful secret in her past: during the war, Marie had an intimate relationship with a German soldier.
The Guardian’s film critic hailed Woman Unknown as “elegantly appointed” in his review, likening it to Alfred Hitchcock’s Rebecca.
Arcel also won the festival’s best actress prize, the Volpi Cup, which puzzled some critics: usually, Venice doesn’t award more than one prize to a film. Speaking to the press after the ceremony, the jury president, Maggie Gyllenhaal, said they were able to make an exception because the jury’s vote for the Danish actor was unanimous. “She is going to blow our socks off,” she said.
![Maggie Gyllenhaal laughing and Pietrangelo Buttafuoco smiling as they both lean towards May el-Toukhy with the Golden Lion](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/10c7c7c95980e31a3c9674c858353e115a4a3788/555_0_5000_4000/master/5000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
In an emotional acceptance speech, El-Toukhy thanked Gyllenhaal for addressing the underrepresentation of female film-makers at the start of the festival. Woman Unknown was the only film in competition to be solely directed by a woman.
“This film has been incredibly challenging to make financially, logistically, emotionally,” El-Toukhy said. “And what kept me going was the urgent need to illuminate the unknown women of our common history, to make them known. And especially tonight, I feel like I succeeded in doing just that.”
![Johnnie To smiles as he presents the grand jury award to a bowing Lee Chang-dong](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/60e57d1229a3b2dad71ffb27e3b1eb7330945794/44_0_3194_2557/master/3194.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The runner-up grand jury prize went to the Korean director Lee Chang-dong’s Possible Love, a simmering tale of an unhappy married couple befriended by a documentary maker and her wealthy husband, which drew rave reviews.
The special jury prize, Venice’s equivalent of a bronze medal, went to Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor’s documentary NAZA, about Israel’s AI-powered mass killing of civilians in Gaza.
The film, which was produced by the Guardian, is based on testimony from 24 Israeli military insiders who are interviewed anonymously at night on rooftops in Tel Aviv. It takes its title from an acronym used by the intelligence service to indicate how many civilians it expects to die in an airstrike on Gaza.
![Rachel Szor and Yuval Abraham standing with the special jury award against spotlights and press photographers](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/17dbce7e7838dabc346930c7a396ae72841db27d/567_0_5000_4000/master/5000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
“It’s honestly not very easy to stand here, thinking of all the Israeli politicians and journalists who are now attacking this film and denying it without even seeing it,” Abraham said when accepting his prize. “So much is being done not to look at reality.”
The day after NAZA’s premiere, the Israeli military “categorically denied” the allegations made in the film.
The Russian director Ilya Khrzhanovsky won the Silver Lion for best director for the visually stunning DAU, a biopic of the Nobel prize-winning quantum physicist Lev Landau, who was pressured into working on the Soviet Union’s nuclear weapons programme.
The inclusion of Khrzhanovsky’s film in the Venice lineup was criticised by the Ukrainian government in the run-up to the festival, over its lead actor Teodor Currentzis’s refusal to condemn the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and for having received funding from a Russian businessman who was later sanctioned by the US and Ukraine.
![Ilya Khrzhanovsky smiles as he balances the Silver Lion award between his hands on his head](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/0cd5d858dbe50bc741c7890fbe2e39261229e2f0/406_0_4316_3453/master/4316.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
DAU was filmed in Kharkiv between 2008 and 2011, before the start of the conflict. At a press conference on the Lido, Khrzhanovsky said: “The only thing I can wish for is peace and success for the Ukrainian government to succeed in the best possible way, to save the country and to win this war.”
John Malkovich took home the Volpi Cup for best actor, for his role as an erratic veteran CIA agent whose cancer diagnosis leads him to question the morality of his profession, in Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine.
after newsletter promotion
The 72-year-old US actor was not present in Venice and accepted his award via a video link. “I am humbled to be chosen for this award, which has been given to so many wonderful actors over the past 83 iterations of the Venice film festival,” Malkovich said.
Full list of winners
Golden Lion for best film: Woman Unknown, directed by May el-Toukhy
Grand jury prize: Possible Love, directed by Lee Chang-dong
Silver Lion for best director: Ilya Khrzhanovsky for DAU
Special jury prize: NAZA, directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor
Best screenplay: Un bon petit soldat (A Good Little Soldier), Stéphane Brizé, Coralie Amédéo, Olivier Gorce
Volpi Cup for best actress: Mathilde Arcel in Woman Unknown
Volpi Cup for best actor: John Malkovich in Wild Horse Nine
Marcello Mastroianni award for best young actor: Malou Khebizi in 15/18 A Place to Heal
Armani Beauty audience award: Eu contez (I Matter), directed by Alina Șerban
Luigi De Laurentiis award for debut film: La maison du vent (House of the Wind), directed by Auguste Bernard Kouemo Yanghu
summary: May el-Toukhy’s film Woman Unknown won the Golden Lion at the Venice film festival, while its star Mathilde Arcel also received the Volpi Cup for best actress. The Gaza documentary NAZA, directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, was awarded the special jury prize. Other major winners included Lee Chang-dong’s Possible Love for the grand jury prize and Ilya Khrzhanovsky for best director.
key_points: May el-Toukhy's Woman Unknown won the Golden Lion as the only film in competition solely directed by a woman.
Mathilde Arcel won the Volpi Cup for best actress for her role in Woman Unknown, an exception to Venice's usual single-prize rule due to a unanimous jury vote.
The Gaza documentary NAZA won the special jury prize amid criticism from Israeli politicians and a categorical denial of its allegations by the Israeli military.
Lee Chang-dong’s Possible Love won the runner-up grand jury prize.
Ilya Khrzhanovsky won the Silver Lion for best director for DAU, a film that faced prior criticism from the Ukrainian government.

title: Céline Dion performs first live show in more than six years
author: Raphael Boyd
content:
Céline Dion wept on stage in Paris as she performed her first live show in more than six years after taking an extended break to deal with her health.
Addressing the sold-out crowd on Saturday, a visibly emotional Dion told them that it was “amazing we are all together”.
She added: “I made a promise. I made a promise to come back and to be back on stage. Here I am singing for you, and singing for me. Thank you so very much for your support, your patience. I am everything I am because you love me.”
![A line of people queueing in the sunshine underneath a bridge.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/49c513b3e1fd258f198fe1a9955b2306712bf379/0_0_5731_3821/master/5731.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
She last performed a full set in 2020 as part of her Courage Tour, but was unable to continue with a planned 2022 North American leg after being diagnosed with stiff person syndrome (SPS) in 2022.
The singer, who is scheduled to perform a residency at the Plenitude Arena in Paris between 12 September 2026 and 29 May 2027, told fans that she “made a promise to come back”.
SPS is a rare autoimmune neurological disorder that often causes muscle stiffness and painful spasms which vary in severity, caused by the body mistakenly attacking healthy nerve cells. There is no known cure for the condition.
After her diagnosis, Dion stepped away from the spotlight and had only briefly performed three times since: at a virtual performance at a charity event for healthcare workers during the Covid pandemic in 2020, at the opening ceremony of the 2024 summer Olympics in Paris, where she sang the Édith Piaf song Hymne à l’amour, and at the conclusion of fashion designer Elie Saab’s show in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, later that same year.
![A woman in a black dress on stage looks out across an audience.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/cb134f3cfc0af150a69868c90deb392e1c268758/0_0_6000_4000/master/6000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
The performance in Paris is the first of 26 shows Dion is slated to perform at the arena, having increased from an initial 10 due to high demand for tickets. Dion first announced her comeback on 30 March, her birthday, with all the tickets for the shows – estimated to be about 1,170,00 – selling out within a few hours of going on sale. More than 9 million fans reportedly tried to buy them.
Dion is expected to perform many of her most popular songs, including her Oscar and Grammy-winning ballad My Heart Will Go On, as well as hits in English and her native French, including It’s All Coming Back to Me Now, The Power of Love and Pour que tu m’aimes encore.
summary: Céline Dion performed her first live show in over six years in Paris after stepping back from touring due to her diagnosis of stiff person syndrome. A visibly emotional Dion thanked her sold-out crowd for their patience and support during her extended health-related break. This concert marks the beginning of an extended arena residency in Paris following overwhelming ticket demand.
key_points: Céline Dion performed her first full live show in over six years in Paris.
She had previously paused touring in 2022 following her diagnosis with stiff person syndrome, a rare autoimmune neurological disorder.
Dion addressed a sold-out crowd, expressing gratitude for their patience and support.
The performance is part of an expanded residency at the Plenitude Arena in Paris.

title: How Céline Dion, 58, is training for her stage comeback – her 5-day strength and mobility routine
author: Hannah Bradfield
content:
Ahead of her highly anticipated return to the stage following a 2022 diagnosis of stiff-person syndrome (SPS), Céline Dion has revealed the workout routine helping her prepare for life back on tour.
The singer, who begins a five-week residency in Paris later this month, told Harper’s Bazaar that she currently does 90-minute Pilates sessions three times a week, alongside two weekly ballet classes with a local dance company.
What is stiff-person syndrome?
Stiff-person syndrome is an extremely rare progressive autoimmune neurological disorder, thought to affect around one or two people per million people, according to Johns Hopkins Medicine.
The condition most commonly causes muscle stiffness and painful spasms that come and go, often worsening over time.
‘Although there is no treatment that cures stiff person syndrome, working with a specialist and maintaining symptom control can make it easier to live with the condition,’ the organisation explains.
The Stiff Person Syndrome UK and Ireland Support Group and Charity notes that people with the condition are often initially misdiagnosed with anxiety or depression, and that women appear to be affected more often than men.
According to Harper’s Bazaar, Dion has undergone physical therapy, vocal therapy and immunotherapy since her diagnosis, alongside taking medication. In 2024, her foundation also donated $2 million towards research into autoimmune neurological disorders.
Why Céline Dion's workout routine makes sense
Dion's current routine combines Pilates and ballet five days a week, placing an emphasis on strength, mobility, balance and control.
While exercise won't be appropriate in the same way for everyone living with stiff-person syndrome, there is some evidence that carefully supervised movement can help with symptom management.
A case report found that therapeutic exercise improved muscle flexibility, balance and functional ability in a woman with the condition.
Meanwhile, another case report found that a clinical Pilates programme had 'positive effects on many physical and functional parameters' in a patient with stiff-person syndrome.
More broadly, Pilates has well-established benefits for many women during midlife.
‘Pilates emphasises correct postural alignment, core strength and muscle balance. It is great for ironing out muscular imbalances, injury rehabilitation and injury prevention,’ Aimee Victoria Long, PT and founder of Body Beautiful Method, previously told Women’s Health.
Ballet offers similar benefits. A 2024 study found that a 10-week classical ballet programme improved strength and balance in women over 50.
And, as Céline Dion demonstrates, it's never too late to begin. She only took up ballet as an adult, yet it has become a key part of the training helping her prepare for her return to performing.
Hannah Bradfield is a Senior Health and Fitness Writer for Women’s Health UK. An NCTJ-accredited journalist, Hannah graduated from Loughborough University with a BA in English and Sport Science and an MA in Media and Cultural Analysis. She has been covering sports, health and fitness for the last five years and has created content for outlets including BBC Sport, BBC Sounds, Runner’s World and Stylist. She especially enjoys interviewing those working within the community to improve access to sport, exercise and wellness. Hannah is a 2024 John Schofield Trust Fellow and was also named a 2022 Rising Star in Journalism by The Printing Charity. A keen runner, Hannah was firmly a sprinter growing up (also dabbling in long jump) but has since transitioned to longer-distance running. While 10K is her favoured race distance, she loves running or volunteering at parkrun every Saturday, followed, of course, by pastries. She’s always looking for fun new runs and races to do and brunch spots to try.
summary: Céline Dion is preparing for her stage comeback and upcoming Paris residency following her 2022 diagnosis of stiff-person syndrome. To ready herself for touring, she follows a five-day weekly fitness routine consisting of three 90-minute Pilates sessions and two ballet classes. Her medical management and recovery efforts have also included physical therapy, vocal therapy, immunotherapy, and medication.
key_points: Céline Dion is preparing for a stage comeback and a five-week residency in Paris.
Her training routine combines 90-minute Pilates sessions three times a week with two weekly ballet classes.
Dion was diagnosed with stiff-person syndrome in 2022, a rare progressive autoimmune neurological disorder.
She has previously undergone physical therapy, vocal therapy, and immunotherapy as part of managing her condition.

title: ‘It’s like failing your driving test’: SNL UK stars on the most brutal job in comedy
author: Lauren Morris
content:
When Sky announced that it was bringing the legendary US sketch show Saturday Night Live to the UK, the public had questions. Would it be British enough? Edgy enough? Cooler than its American cousin?
The answer was emphatically delivered in week one when the cast performed a Hamnet parody, in which William Shakespeare returned to his family from London on a Lime scooter with a mild ketamine addiction and a “c***y little earring”. It was deeply British, a touch provocative, and extremely funny.
To get the sketch into the show, the cast had to talk to Sky and “have almost like a board meeting in the hallway about getting ‘c***y’ in, and the meaning of that”, says Jack Shep, who played a Brat-ified version of the bard. He had to explain how the word had become positive slang in Gen Z culture. “It was awesome. We were like, ‘It’s different now!’ That was week one, so that tells you everything you need to know.”
![Jack Shep as a Brat-ified William Shakespeare in one of the show's first sketches](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/09/09/10/22/01_29_SNL_UK_S01.jpeg)
Since then, the sketch show has continued to venture near the knuckle when searching for the nation’s funny bone – from skewering former prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor over his Jeffrey Epstein links to the Muppet-esque portrayal of Keir Starmer – and it’s worked. SNL UK received a warm – and relieved – reception from viewers and critics alike after its first run, while its sketches have been watched over 54 million times on YouTube since it premiered in March. National treasures Louis Theroux and Martin Lewis even made cameos as themselves in various skits.
Tonight, the show is back for more, just four months after the first series came to an end. No one is more surprised than its cast of rising stars – many of whom had been warned that attempting to bring the live sketch show to a hard-to-please, ever sceptical Britain would be a disaster. “We have been spoken to by pretty much everyone in the industry who told us why it was gonna be bad,” says Paddy Young, who co-hosts the Weekend Update segment. “A poisoned chalice, that’s what I got told. But it makes me feel very patriotic. How else would this country respond to something that’s high risk like this? Of course, we’re just going to say it’s going to be bad.”
![Emma Sidi, Ania Magliano and Paddy Young during the Weekend Update segment](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/09/09/10/03/03_18_SNL_UK_S01.jpg)
“People were like, ‘I think it was… good?’” Shep says of SNL UK’s first show. “It’s like we were waiting to hear a gunshot but we haven’t heard one. It’s been really nice. We obviously had supporters from early on, but I think everyone was very sceptical.”
Sitting across from the cast in a London hotel while they’re in junket mode, it’s clear to see that the doubters never needed to worry. Watching them fire jokes back and forth between one another feels like securing front-row tickets to the Wimbledon of comedy, with their electric rapport leaving me with mild whiplash (or rather, quiplash).
Surely those comedy sceptics must be eating their words? “A lot of them are dead,” Shep jokes, with Young quickly adding: “Yeah. Coincidence?”
Even fellow cast member Emma Sidi wasn’t sure the format would work in the UK until the first show aired. “I couldn’t see the laughter working in the room as well as it does,” she admits. “I think that’s only because we haven’t had a big comedy show with a live studio audience be successful in the UK for such a long time. I had a disconnect of even imagining a room full of British people laughing. In my head, it was either a dated thing or an American thing – but then we were like, it can work.”
![Larry Dean as King Charles, George Fouracres as Keir Starmer, Celeste Dring as Angela Rayner, Emma Sidi as Queen Camilla and Jack Shep as a flight attendant in a sketch](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/09/09/10/06/06_23_SNL_UK_S01.jpg)
After 16 weeks off – during which the show’s stars and its extensive team of writers have been performing at the Edinburgh Fringe, cramming in holidays and rearranging tour dates – they’re all ready to return. Although given sketches are pitched on a week-by-week basis for each Saturday’s particular celebrity host, there’s not much they could do to prepare over the summer.
“It’s hard to prep material in advance,” says star Celeste Dring, who spent the time off hiring an accountant and moving flats. “You need to be around everyone and you need some feedback on what’s working, what’s not working.”
Young, who teases that he may or may not be reprising the role of now-prime minister Andy Burnham (although he may have to shave that impressive ’tache), admits that “a smart person” would have brushed up his impressions ahead of series two, but he didn’t. Instead, he’s been recovering after slicing open his finger with a samurai sword – which actually sounds like a great idea for a sketch.
“I’m in physio and I can only do that,” he says, while trying to bend the injured finger. “It builds character. The thing with hands is they’re overrated. Once you lose one, you think, ‘God, I don’t need that for anything. I don’t want to open a bottle of Pepsi…or Coke or Dr Pepper.” Briefly dropping into an eerily accurate impersonation of US president Donald Trump, he adds: “‘We love the lilt!’ I have been practising a few impressions, I guess. That’s Angela Rayner by the way.”
![Louis Theroux made a cameo in the final episode of SNL UK's first series](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/09/09/10/46/08_18_SNL_UK_S01.jpg)
Meanwhile, Sidi spent the time off getting to know her baby son, who she welcomed last year with husband and SNL UK writer Al Roberts. “I wasn’t really able to do that during the last series,” she says. “I saw him learn to walk and I was a bit nervous that I’d be busy doing the show while he did that, but he did it in front of me so that’s great.”
The comedy couple will be doing the “crazy juggle” between work and parenting once again when they return to what Sidi describes as “Hogwarts for comedy”, but it does mean that they get to spend some quality time together. “This is a really weird way of dating,” she giggles. “We’re at work together, talking about comedy, without a baby.”
A typical week at SNL UK isn’t for the faint of heart; the cast and writers pitch sketches on a Monday, then plan sets, costumes and scripts all week before performing what can often be a completely different version of the skit on Saturday night. They get the Sunday off before starting all over again with new ideas for another celebrity host on Monday.
The cast are still getting used to watching their jokes, some of which they’ve been developing and working on all week, be savagely cut after Saturday afternoon’s dress rehearsal. “The second a sketch gets cut, you go, ‘I’m devastated.’ But then you go, ‘I know why – it wasn’t good enough’,” Sidi says. “It’s like doing your driving test every week and failing every week and rebooking every week. That’s what it feels like doing SNL. It is really fun, but it is brutal. There’s no two ways about it. But you just need to rebook that driving test – don’t give up. You will learn to drive.”
It’s the same for the show’s Weekend Update segment, where Young and co-anchor Ania Magliano deliver quickfire jokes about the week’s biggest news stories. “When you’re churning out ideas and most of them just by their very nature don’t work, that is such a weird thing,” Young says. “A show might go well on Saturday and then you have one day off and on Monday, you’re back to being crap all over again. It’s really humbling.”
While the likes of Tina Fey, Jamie Dornan, Hannah Waddingham and Ncuti Gatwa were the first celebrity hosts to take a chance on SNL’s British cousin, Jurassic Park star Jeff Goldblum is kicking off series two tonight with CMAT as his musical guest. Despite just how physically and mentally tiring making the show can be, its cast – which recently welcomed comedian and Such Brave Girls star Freddie Meredith into their ranks – can’t wait to return for their sophomore year and the sketch madness that’ll come with it.
For Young, it’s all worth it for the curtain call at the end of each live show, where the celebrity host and full cast take to the stage as the credits start to roll. “When we’re all waiting to go on for the bow and normally we’re all wearing whatever the last costume is, that’s always pretty sweet,” he says. “It’s just surreal to see Louis Theroux standing next to some Beefeaters. You see that and you think, ‘That’s why I got into this game’.”
‘Saturday Night Live UK’ returns tonight at 10pm on Sky One
summary: Saturday Night Live UK is returning to Sky One for its second series after a surprisingly successful and well-received first run. Despite being warned by industry insiders that the high-risk format would fail in Britain, the show attracted millions of YouTube views and positive reviews. The cast describes the demanding weekly schedule of pitching, rehearsing, and cutting sketches as a brutal yet rewarding process.
key_points: SNL UK's first series received a warm reception from viewers and critics, garnering over 54 million YouTube views after premiering in March.
Despite industry warnings that the live sketch format was a 'poisoned chalice' for British audiences, the show successfully tackled topical subjects and featured high-profile cameos.
The rigorous weekly production cycle involves pitching on Monday and reshaping material throughout the week before performing live on Saturday.
Cast member Emma Sidi likened the grueling process of developing and frequently cutting sketches to 'failing your driving test every week and rebooking.'
Series two premieres tonight with celebrity host Jeff Goldblum and musical guest CMAT.

title: Red Hot Raw Star Internally Viewed As 'Future WWE Champion' (WWE News)
author: Jamie Kennedy
content:
![WWE Raw 946 OTM Royce Keys Lucien Price Bronco Nima](https://d2thvodm3xyo6j.cloudfront.net/media/2026/09/3a428e69ab21cba2f790a9303aa2fa0c.jpg) 
WKRD Wrestling and False Finish are reporting that Royce Keys could be heading straight to the top of the industry as a future WWE Champion. WKRD got the ball rolling on the good news by writing about some heavy praise sent Royce's way by members of upper management - Triple H and other bosses are impressed by what Keys has been doing on Raw since teaming with Lucien Price and Bronco Nima as 946.
Then, False Finish chimed in to say there are even talks about Royce going all the way and becoming the company's main man. A WWE Title reign certainly isn't out of the question someday. That's how Keys is internally viewed by those making the big decisions. It's looking likely he'll win either the WWE Title or World Heavyweight Championship going forwards.
Of course, there's no definitive timescale on that. It could well be a general statement being tossed around during creative meetings: 'Let's make Royce Keys World Champ sometime'. That sort of thing. However, it's a huge upswing for the man creatively that he's even being discussed in that sort of way.
Keys had been treading water as a babyface, but his stable with Price and Nima carries an edge, and their repeated attacks on The Bloodline have turned some heads.
Ex-AEW star Royce debuted during the Royal Rumble match earlier this year, but he struggled to get going until recently. SmackDown wasn't exactly kind to Keys, but he's fared much better since jumping to Raw and leading his own crew.
Next stop: Top WWE titles?
summary: Reports from WKRD Wrestling and False Finish indicate that Royce Keys is viewed internally by WWE management, including Triple H, as a future world champion. Keys has gained significant momentum since moving to Raw and forming the stable 946 with Lucien Price and Bronco Nima. Although there is no definitive timeline for a title win, his recent creative upswing follows attacks on The Bloodline.
key_points: Upper management, including Triple H, is highly impressed with Royce Keys' recent performance on Raw.
Internal discussions have raised the possibility of Keys eventually winning the WWE Title or World Heavyweight Championship.
Keys' career improved significantly after jumping to Raw and forming the stable 946 with Lucien Price and Bronco Nima.
The stable has turned heads with their repeated attacks on The Bloodline.

title: Lil Durk: Grammy-winning US rapper acquitted in murder-for-hire trial
author: Tinshui Yeung
content:
![Lil Durk wearing sunglasses and a multi-coloured suit, and holding up the gold gramophone-shaped Grammy Award](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/42bf/live/4e811660-ae77-11f1-b1d1-571ed4d7ff2c.jpg)
Lil Durk holding the Grammy Award he won for best melodic rap performance in 2024
- Published
Grammy-winning rapper Lil Durk was acquitted on Friday of all charges in a federal murder-for-hire case accusing him of orchestrating the revenge killing of a man shot dead in a daytime ambush in Los Angeles four years ago.
The Chicago rapper was arrested in 2024 and accused of involvement in a shooting that killed the cousin of rival rapper Quando Rondo.
Defence lawyer Drew Findling said the recording artist, whose real name is Durk Devontay Banks, was "thankful" following the verdict.
Lil Durk has had seven albums in the US Billboard chart's top five since 2019 and has also collaborated with stars including Drake and J Cole on hit singles.
Supporters cheered outside a Los Angeles courthouse after the verdict, which came following three days of jury deliberations.
The 33-year-old faced five felony counts, including murder for hire resulting in death and conspiracy. If convicted, he could have faced a life sentence.
Although Banks was found not guilty of the charges in the case, he remains in custody and faces a separate trial on 5 October, where he will face racketeering murder and firearms charges.
"While we are disappointed with the jury's decision regarding Durk Banks, a.k.a. 'Lil Durk,' we look forward to presenting our evidence at his second trial", First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said in a statement.
In the three-week trial, two co-defendants were tried alongside Banks. Deandre "OTF Dede" Wilson and David "Browneyez" Lindsey were convicted of stalking and conspiracy to commit stalking, but acquitted of murder-for-hire charges, the BBC's US partner CBS News reports, external.
The trial relied on three co-operating witnesses, Kavon "OTF Vonnie" Grant, Keith "Flacka" Jones and Kacey "OTF Jam" Hester, who reached plea deals and testified against Banks, Wilson and Lindsey.
It stemmed from a fatal shooting in August 2022 at a petrol station in Los Angeles, where a car carrying Rondo, whose real name is Tyquian Bowman, was shot at. Bowman was unharmed, but his cousin Saviay'a Robinson, who was also in the car, was killed.
Federal prosecutors accused Banks of plotting to kill Bowman, in retaliation for the earlier murder of Chicago OTF rapper King Von, who was signed to OTF. Von was killed in 2020 during an early-morning exchange of gunfire in Atlanta.
A friend of Bowman was charged with King Von's murder, but the charges were later dropped. Bowman was not arrested or charged.
Authorities said Banks made it known that he would "pay a bounty" to anyone who killed Bowman. Prosecutors argued that Banks felt pressure on social media to avenge Von's death.
Banks founded OTF in 2010. He won the 2024 Grammy Award for Best Melodic Rap Performance for his single "All My Life" featuring J Cole. He has also been nominated for a Grammy three other times.
summary: Grammy-winning rapper Lil Durk was acquitted of all charges in a federal murder-for-hire trial stemming from a 2022 daytime ambush in Los Angeles that killed a rival rapper's cousin. Despite the not-guilty verdict, he remains in custody to face a separate racketeering murder and firearms trial scheduled for October 5. Two co-defendants were convicted of stalking and conspiracy but acquitted of the murder-for-hire charges.
key_points: Lil Durk was acquitted on Friday of five felony counts, including murder-for-hire resulting in death and conspiracy.
The case involved the August 2022 fatal shooting of Saviay'a Robinson, the cousin of rival rapper Quando Rondo, at a Los Angeles petrol station.
Lil Durk remains in custody to face a separate trial on racketeering murder and firearms charges starting October 5.
Two co-defendants tried alongside him were convicted of stalking and conspiracy to commit stalking.
The 33-year-old artist won a Grammy Award in 2024 for Best Melodic Rap Performance for his single 'All My Life'.

title: Lady Gaga ‘welcomes first baby with fiancé Michael Polansky’
author: Rachel McGrath
content:
Lady Gaga has welcomed her first baby with fiancé Michael Polansky, according to reports.
The couple, who began dating in 2019 and got engaged in March 2024, have kept a low-profile in recent months.
But new images published by US publication Page Six show the pair on a walk in California with Gaga, real name Stefani Joanne Angelina Germanotta, carrying a baby.
Before this, the “Abracadabra” singer had not been pictured publicly since August, when she stopped to take a selfie with a fan. Gaga finished her latest tour, the 86-date Mayhem Ball, in April.
The 40-year-old star has frequently discussed her desire to be a mother, telling the New York Times in March last year: “I’m excited to be a mom. I used to have a lot of apprehension about it.
“The thing that’s the most important to me is to not force my children to live a life that they are not choosing. So the more that we can give them space to discover who they are on their own, that’s the thing that I believe in the most.”
Appearing on The Stephen Colbert Show in October 2025, she said: “I would like to do many things. “All of these things are open. But, what I really want, is to be a mom. That’s my next starring role, I hope.”
Gaga met entrepreneur Polansky, 42, at a friend’s birthday party in late 2019. The pair went Instagram official in February 2020, after being spotted at the Super Bowl together.
The singer then sparked engagement rumours when she was spotted wearing a huge diamond ring in April 2024, and went on to confirm that Polansky had got down on one knee in a video filmed at the Paris Olympics.
The clip showed Gaga meeting French prime minister Gabriel Attal and introducing her partner as “my fiancé”.
Gaga later opened up about the romance to Vogue, describing Polansky as “so smart and so kind”. “And his life and my life are very different,” she continued. “He’s a very private guy and he’s not with me for any other reason than that we are right for each other.
“But I think what I want my fans to know is that I’m just, like, so happy. I’m healthy.”
The Independent has contacted the Lady Gaga’s representative for comment.
summary: Reports indicate that Lady Gaga and her fiancé, Michael Polansky, have welcomed their first child together after being spotted walking in California with a baby. The couple began dating in 2019 and got engaged in March 2024. Gaga has frequently expressed her strong desire to become a mother in previous interviews.
key_points: Lady Gaga and fiancé Michael Polansky have reportedly welcomed their first child.
The couple was photographed by Page Six on a walk in California with a baby.
Gaga and Polansky began dating in 2019 and became engaged in 2024.
The singer has previously expressed a strong desire to become a mother in multiple interviews.

title: 'The Gentlemen' Season 2 Loses Half A Million Viewers In The UK
author: Jake Kanter
content:
!['The Gentlemen' Season 2](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/The-Gentlemen-season-2-e1789122162936.jpg?w=681&h=383&crop=1) 
The blaze of Meghan Markle-shaped publicity around The Gentlemen appears to have done little for the show’s UK ratings, according to official figures.
Season 2 of Guy Ritchie‘s glossy crime drama premiered on September 3 on Netflix and, after seven days of streaming, the first episode was watched by 3 million British viewers.
The Gentlemen‘s viewing figures dropped around 15% from Season 1’s debut episode, which was streamed by an audience of 3.5 million in March 2024.
The ratings were supplied by Overnights.tv via Barb, the UK’s official TV audience body. The figures differ from Netflix’s data, which measures views rather than viewers.
Despite the differing data points, the downward decline in Netflix views was similar. Deadline’s Katie Campione reported that The Gentlemen scored 6.7 million streams in its first four days of availability.
Watch on Deadline
That put it at No. 3 on Netflix’s English TV list from August 31 to September 6, but the series is facing nearly a 50% audience decline in its opening weekend versus Season 1’s premiere viewership.
This trend is not unique to The Gentlemen. Many of the streamer’s continuing series have not been able to attract the same audience as Season 1, including huge hits like Wednesday.
The Gentlemen has already been renewed for a third season amid wild speculation about Markle joining the cast. The Duchess’ arrival has not been confirmed or denied by Netflix and The Gentlemen team.
The Gentlemen stars Theo James as Eddie Horniman, who unexpectedly inherits his father’s sizeable country estate – only to discover it’s part of a cannabis empire.
summary: Season 2 of Guy Ritchie's crime drama 'The Gentlemen' premiered on Netflix in the UK, drawing 3 million viewers for its first episode after seven days. This represents a roughly 15% decline from the debut of Season 1, while opening weekend streams saw a nearly 50% drop compared to the previous season's premiere. Despite this ratings decline, the series has already been renewed for a third season.
key_points: Season 2 of 'The Gentlemen' premiered on Netflix on September 3.
The first episode was watched by 3 million British viewers in its first seven days, according to Barb figures.
Viewership dropped about 15% compared to the Season 1 debut, which had 3.5 million viewers.
Opening weekend streams faced nearly a 50% decline compared to Season 1's premiere.
The series has already been renewed for a third season amidst speculation regarding Meghan Markle joining the cast.

title: Big Brother unveils brand-new 2026 house transformation ahead of launch show
author: Sam Warner
content:
Big Brother has unveiled its house for the 2026 season, which is due to launch this weekend. While we're yet to be introduced to the new contestants who will occupy the house for the next few weeks, the show has shared the all-important look.
The first pictures depict dark maroon-red, blue, green and wood tones, while the new Diary Room chair takes on the iconic eye logo shape once again.
The series returns on ITV this Sunday, and beforehand will undertake a first as content creators The Bov Boys – who include Angryginge – move in for a livestreamed "dry run" of the house over 24 hours.
Related: Best streaming services
Fans can expect "maximum mayhem", with the collective "keeping the team on their toes and putting the House to the test in a way they certainly won’t have anticipated".
The new season has also enlisted show legend Kate Lawler and influencer GK Barry to host new companion show Big Brother: The Group Chat, which broadcasts after the main show on ITV2, ITVX and YouTube.
Elsewhere, Digital Spy recently caught up with hosts AJ Odudu and Will Best, the former teasing of the new season: "Well, first of all, it's going to be the biggest, longest series in this iteration of Big Brother ever.
"So we've got eight exciting weeks, which is really, really brilliant!", Will adding: "More of us. More housemates. Yeah. So that's one big thing."
The latter further said: "We've been assured by the powers that be that this series really is going to be bigger and better than anything that we've done on ITV so far."
"The story unfolds every single night. It's live. Everyone's under surveillance constantly," AJ continued. "And so, the beautiful thing about this show is that the story unfolds as we see it. So, we're all being part of the history that I've no doubt it will make."
Big Brother returns on 13 September at 9pm on ITV2 and ITVX. Big Brother: The Group Chat will air on ITV2, ITVX and YouTube, with episodes also available across major podcast platforms.

title: The Voice UK: Alesha Dixon and Stacey Solomon joing show as ITV confirms revamp
author: Steven McIntosh
content:
![Stacey Solomon and Alesha Dixon](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/840a/live/ba1eec50-ade9-11f1-b1d1-571ed4d7ff2c.jpg)
Solomon and Dixon will replace Emma Willis, who is leaving The Voice to front Strictly Come Dancing
- Published
Alesha Dixon and Stacey Solomon are to host The Voice UK as part of a revamp of the show announced by ITV.
The pair replace Emma Willis, who has presented the singing contest since 2014 but recently left to front the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing.
ITV also confirmed earlier reports that singer Cheryl and rapper Aitch will join the The Voice as coaches, sitting in the show's famous giant red chairs.
It comes after Sir Tom Jones said earlier this week that he had been removed from the series despite wanting to stay, over an insurance issue.
On Friday, the network said: "ITV would like to thank the irreplaceable Sir Tom Jones for all his years on The Voice UK, and the countless incredible and unforgettable moments he gave the show.
"He has brought joy to audiences, and to every singer who performed for him and with him."
The changes will take effect from the next series, which began filming on Friday. The series currently airing on ITV was filmed in 2025.
Destiny's Child singer Kelly Rowland will remain on The Voice coaching panel, alongside Black Eyed Peas frontman Will.I.Am, who has been on the show since its first series.
![Sir Tom Jones, wearing a blue jacket, pictured being interviewed next to Will.I.Am, who is wearing a brown jacket, sunglasses and a red hat](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/96b7/live/d8f992e0-adfa-11f1-8169-6fdea7f79791.jpg)
Sir Tom Jones, pictured with Will.I.Am, said he was "not thrilled" to be offered a reduced role on the show
On Wednesday, Sir Tom, 86, said in a statement he had been offered a "much-reduced role" on the series, which he was "not thrilled about".
"The reason given is because of a financial difficulty with insurance," he added. "They now say in the press they wanted to 'refresh' the show, and with a new coaching line-up there wouldn't be a chair for me."
He concluded: "The only thing I know right now is that there's never a good time to fire an 86-year-old who's still pretty good at his job."
Cheryl launched her career with pop group Girls Aloud and later had several chart hits as a solo artist. She has recorded several songs with Will.I.Am.
She also served as a judge on ITV's The X Factor when the singing competition was at the peak of its popularity in the late 2000s.
Aitch is a Manchester-born rapper whose hits include Rain, Baby, War and Taste (Make It Shake).
"Fusing legendary industry experience with a vibrant competitive spirit, our latest panel of icons is ready to discover and celebrate the most remarkable and exciting vocal talent emerging from every corner of the country," ITV said.
Dixon shot to fame as a member of girl group Mis-Teeq and has served as judge on Strictly Come Dancing and Britain's Got Talent.
She has previously hosted The Greatest Dancer and the Eurovision Song Contest when it was hosted by the UK in Liverpool in 2023.
Solomon came second on The X Factor in 2009, and is now known for hosting Sort Your Life Out and appearing on reality show Stacey & Joe with her husband Joe Swash.
Double Willis
Earlier this year, it was reported that McFly stars Tom Fletcher and Danny Jones would also not be returning to The Voice, after they shared a chair as joint coaches for the last two series.
On Friday, ITV said: "We thank Emma Willis, Tom Fletcher and Danny Jones for their brilliant contributions, and who all brought so much dedication, expertise and energy to The Voice UK and wish them the very best of luck as they embark on their next chapters."
Willis will still be seen on screen for the rest of the current series of The Voice UK, as it was recorded last year.
That means viewers will see Willis hosting two different Saturday night prime-time shows this autumn, for BBC One and ITV.
She will front the new series of the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing from 19 September, alongside comedian Josh Widdicombe and dancer Johannes Radebe.
The trio replace Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman, who left at the end of the previous series.
![Cheryl performs during Manchester Pride 2019 on August 25, 2019 in Manchester, Engla](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/baac/live/ee2ef4c0-adfa-11f1-8169-6fdea7f79791.jpg)
Cheryl shot to fame with Girls Aloud and has also served as a judge on ITV's The X Factor
The Voice launched its UK version in 2012, hosted by Holly Willoughby and Reggie Yates, after the format was successful in the US.
Willis took over presenting duties in 2014, joined for several series by Marvin Humes of boyband JLS. The show jumped from the BBC to ITV in 2017.
The show differs from other singing competitions in that the coaches have their backs turned to contestants as they audition.
If the coaches like a contestant's voice, they can spin around in their chairs to see their identity and offer to mentor them during the series.
Other previous coaches on the UK series include Olly Murs, Jennifer Hudson, Kylie Minogue, Rita Ora, Anne Marie and LeAnn Rimes.

- ![Josh Widdicombe, Emma Willis and Johannes Radebe](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/d803/live/a172de70-538d-11f1-b682-cf91850925ea.jpg)
- ![Johannes Radebe, Josh Widdicombe and Emma Willis smiling together in smart, presenting clothes](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/eccb/live/d5b3ae30-ad1f-11f1-826f-933990eae6f0.jpg)
  - Published25 July
 ![Claudia Winkleman pictured on her chat show](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/e0fe/live/09c4e010-8519-11f1-bf4e-6b2bb6027b0a.jpg)
summary: ITV has announced a major revamp for The Voice UK, with Alesha Dixon and Stacey Solomon replacing long-time host Emma Willis. Willis has left the show to present BBC's Strictly Come Dancing. Additionally, singer Cheryl and rapper Aitch are joining the coaching panel, while Sir Tom Jones and joint coaches Tom Fletcher and Danny Jones will not return.
key_points: Alesha Dixon and Stacey Solomon are the new hosts of The Voice UK.
Emma Willis left the show to front BBC's Strictly Come Dancing.
Cheryl and Aitch are joining the coaching panel alongside returning coaches Kelly Rowland and Will.I.Am.
Sir Tom Jones stated he was removed from the series due to insurance issues and a desire to refresh the show.

title: Hilary Duff at the O2 Arena is actually what dreams are made of – review
author: Adam White
content:
To witness Hilary Duff selling out London’s O2 Arena in 2026, twice, is a bit like witnessing a flash mob on your way to work, or somebody eating a pack of 3D Doritos. What time machine have you inadvertently gained access to? What century is this? But Duff’s resurgence is as much to do with cultural nostalgia as it is the power of clean living.
An artist who has – to her credit, really – never once set foot outside her lane of soft, beachy, featherlight pop, Duff carries a spotless rap sheet and the same grinning radiance that made her a star in the first place. Duff definitely exhibited snippets of bite in her heyday (remember her funny if now quietly tragic love triangle with Aaron Carter and Lindsay Lohan, or her feud with Faye Dunaway?), but she was more or less strictly PG: the Y2K Disney queen that parents actually wanted their daughters to turn out like.
That explains why her show tonight – the first of two London dates on her first major tour since 2008 – feels like such a love-in. The crowd is a mix of thirtysomething girls and gays and it’s-wine-o-clock mums, all seemingly with rich emotional ties to the now 38-year-old actor-slash-pop star. So the uninitiated will likely be baffled by much of it, from the wand Duff produces to draw Mickey Mouse ears in mid-air (a throwback to her old Disney Channel ads), to the gasps that greet a fan who takes to the stage wearing a version of Duff’s white ballgown and distractingly tiny mask from her cult 2004 romcom A Cinderella Story.
It all conjures a sometimes strange mix of sincerity and wink-wink irony, with Duff gamely going along with the lightly withering memes and fashion throwback TikToks that have helped propel her into the spotlight again. “What Dreams Are Made Of” from The Lizzie McGuire Movie – which she sang in that film with her own Italian doppelganger – is more of a gag than a serious banger, yet it serves as the grand finale here. And at one point she invites 10 fans up on stage to recreate a particularly listless and robotic bit of choreography from one of her old live performances that went viral a few years ago. When life gives you lemons, I suppose.
Still, Duff is such a preternaturally upbeat performer that it’d be tricky to not be won over by all of the above. She speaks eloquently of her LGTBQ+ fans at one point, and appears misty-eyed upon first seeing the sheer number of people here tonight. Her voice is limited but pretty, and she can still authentically sell the plucky naivety of early bubblegum singles “Anywhere But Here”, “Wake Up” and “So Yesterday”, all of which produce the night’s most plainly pleasurable moments.
Lovely, too, are the melancholy if undeniably Swiftian cuts from her recent album Luck… or Something, like the older-boyfriend kiss-off “Mature”, and the sombre seven-year-itch number “Roommates”. That much of the crowd sings along to both suggests that, despite appearances to the contrary, this isn’t a purely “2003 or nothing” affair.
summary: Hilary Duff sold out London's O2 Arena for her first major tour since 2008, drawing a nostalgic crowd of thirtysomething fans and mums. The concert blended her signature PG bubblegum pop hits with self-aware internet meme throwbacks and newer, more melancholy material from her album Luck... or Something. Despite her limited vocal range, Duff's upbeat and genuine stage presence easily won over the audience.
key_points: Hilary Duff sold out London's O2 Arena twice for her first major tour since 2008.
The audience consisted largely of thirtysomething fans, LGBTQ+ supporters, and wine-o-clock mums.
The concert featured nostalgic elements like her classic Disney Channel hits alongside wink-wink internet meme throwbacks.
Duff also performed newer, more somber tracks from her album Luck... or Something, which the crowd sang along to.

![](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-hollywoodreporter-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
![Sandra Bullock as Sally Owens and Nicole Kidman as Gillian Owens in Practical Magic 2, a Warner Bros. Pictures release.](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/rev-1-PM2-TP-067_High_Res_JPEG-H-2026.jpg?w=1296&h=730&crop=1) 
After six weeks with Spider-Man: Brand New Day at the top of the domestic box office, Practical Magic 2 looks to conjure up a victory.
Warner Bros. Pictures‘ Practical Magic 2 debuts in over 4,000 theaters and arrives 28 years after Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman originated their roles as the Owens sisters in the first film. The studio projects director Susanne Bier‘s feature to gross between $30 million and $35 million from North America in its opening weekend, with an additional $18 million to $23 million overseas.
The initial movie collected a total of $46 million domestically from its theatrical run that began Oct. 16, 1998, meaning that the sequel has a chance to surpass this in its debut frame. Adapting the work of author Alice Hoffman, Practical Magic 2 centers on witches Sally (Bullock) and Gillian (Kidman), who aim to break the curse that has prevented their family members from finding love. Joey King, Maisie Williams and Lee Pace round out the cast.
Related Stories
![Lily James and Jack Reynor](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-hollywoodreporter-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
![Paul Greengrass](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-hollywoodreporter-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
Critics have not felt the film’s magic, as the sequel holds a 36 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. In her review for The Hollywood Reporter, critic Angie Han wrote that the movie “works better the less you look for any sense of logic, and the more you just lean into the transient joys of watching these [two] actresses bounce off each other.”
![](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-hollywoodreporter-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif) 
Sony Pictures’ Spider-Man: Brand New Day has led the domestic box office for six consecutive weeks, but that streak will come to an end this weekend.
Still, the Tom Holland-led film that hails from Marvel Studios continues to make its mark, as the record-setting movie is on its way to becoming the top title on the all-time North American chart. The feature is expected to soon surpass the $936 million domestic total for 2015’s Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens, which should happen either this weekend or the following one.
Also opening this weekend are Angel’s Runner, starring Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson; Focus Features’ Andrew Garfield-led The Uprising; and Inaugural’s The Fix, with Liam Neeson and Zachary Levi.

The sequel arrives 28 years after the original film, with studio projections placing its North American opening weekend between $30 million and $35 million. Meanwhile, critics have given the movie a 36 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.
